entries.name: Blender

licence.name: GPL-2.0-or-later for the source (binaries distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later; some modules Apache-2.0)

engines.name: Cycles
engines.does: Path-tracing render engine with CPU and GPU backends (CUDA, OptiX, HIP, oneAPI, Metal), adaptive sampling, denoising, baking and light linking.

engines.name: EEVEE
engines.does: Rasterizing real-time render engine that reads the same shader nodes as Cycles; used for the interactive viewport and for final renders.

engines.name: Geometry Nodes
engines.does: Node-based procedural system with fields, instances, simulation zones, baking and node-based tools.

engines.name: Sculpt mode
engines.does: Brush-based sculpting with 32 brush types, masks, dynamic topology and multiresolution levels.

engines.name: Curves sculpt (hair)
engines.does: Brush-based grooming of hair curves.

engines.name: Grease Pencil
engines.does: Stroke objects for 2D drawing and animation in 3D space.

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: Rigid body, cloth, soft body, fluid (liquid and gas), particles and force fields.

engines.name: Armatures and Rigify
engines.does: Bone rigs with IK, constraints, shape keys and drivers; Rigify generates control rigs from rig-type building blocks.

engines.name: Video Sequencer
engines.does: Video editing system for arranging clips, transitions and audio.

engines.name: Compositor
engines.does: Node-based image compositing of renders and passes.

engines.name: Movie Clip tracking
engines.does: Marker tracking, camera and object solving, plane tracks and 2D stabilization.

capabilities.does: Copies the selected vertices, edges or faces and keeps the copy joined to the original, so edges turn into faces and a face grows into a block. Motion can be limited to one axis; faces move along their averaged normal by default.
capabilities.inputs: selected vertices, edges or faces in Edit Mode; optional axis

capabilities.does: Rounds selected edges or corners by replacing them with new faces. Options: width mode (Offset, Width, Depth, Percent, Absolute), segment count, profile shape, miter style for outer and inner corners, overlap clamping, normal hardening and face strength.
capabilities.inputs: selected vertices or edges; width, segments, profile shape
capabilities.outputs: bevelled geometry with new faces and edges

capabilities.does: Creates a border of new faces inside the selected faces. Options set border thickness and depth, grow the border outward, inset each face on its own, follow existing edges (Edge Rail), keep width even, and interpolate UVs and colours.
capabilities.outputs: inner faces plus a ring of border faces

capabilities.does: Inserts one or more evenly spaced edge loops across a ring of faces, previewed as the cursor moves over an edge. The loop ends at poles where the face loop stops. A UV-correction option limits texture distortion.
capabilities.inputs: an edge under the cursor; Number of Cuts

capabilities.does: Combines or subtracts a second mesh, or a collection of meshes, from the modified mesh. Operations: Intersect, Union, Difference. Solvers: Float (fast, no overlap support), Exact (handles overlap, slow) and Manifold (fastest, needs manifold meshes).
capabilities.inputs: modified mesh plus an object or collection operand

capabilities.does: Mirrors a mesh across its local X, Y or Z axes, or across another object's position and rotation. It can cut the mesh at the plane (Bisect), merge or clip vertices at the plane, and mirror UVs and left/right vertex groups.

Makes copies of geometry along a line, a circle, a curve or a custom transform. Settings cover count or distance, offsets, rotation alignment, random offset, rotation and scale with a seed, and merging nearby vertices after the instances are realized.
capabilities.inputs: geometry; shape, count or distance, offsets
capabilities.outputs: many copies, as instances or real geometry

capabilities.does: Splits each face into smaller faces to smooth a mesh with the Catmull-Clark or Simple algorithm, with separate levels for viewport and render. Extras: edge creases, UV and boundary smoothing, custom normals, and Cycles adaptive subdivision by pixel size or edge length.

Reduces the face count in three modes: Collapse (ratio, symmetry, vertex-group weighting), Un-Subdivide (undoes grid-like subdivision over a set number of iterations) and Planar (dissolves flat areas under an angle limit, with delimit options for seams, materials, UVs and sharp edges).
capabilities.inputs: mesh; mode and ratio or angle limit
capabilities.outputs: lighter mesh with a shown face count

capabilities.does: Keeps several subdivision levels on one mesh so detail can be sculpted at a chosen level. Buttons add smooth, simple or linear levels, unsubdivide, rebuild subdivisions from a sculpt, reshape, apply base and save displacements externally. It bakes normal or displacement maps.

Moves each vertex onto the surface of a target mesh. Wrap methods: Nearest Surface Point, Project (along chosen axes, with cull and distance limit), Nearest Vertex and Target Normal Project. Snap mode, offset and a vertex group refine the result.
capabilities.inputs: object to wrap; target mesh; vertex group
capabilities.outputs: deformed object lying on the target

capabilities.does: Deforms an object through a lattice cage object. An optional vertex group limits the effect and a strength factor blends the original and deformed positions. The base can be a mesh, curve, surface, text, lattice or particles.
capabilities.inputs: base object; lattice object; vertex group; strength

capabilities.does: Rebuilds the original mesh data as uniform topology on a voxel grid and removes inner self-intersecting geometry. Controls: voxel size, adaptivity, pole fixing and volume preservation; masks, face sets and colour attributes can carry over.

QuadriFlow-based remesh that builds a quad mesh from an existing mesh. Settings: symmetry, sharp-feature and boundary preservation, attribute transfer, smooth normals, a target given as ratio, edge length or face count, and a seed that changes the quad layout.

Manual retopology draws a new mesh over a source mesh. A retopology overlay shows the original through the new surface, Poly Build adds, changes and removes faces, and snapping sticks new vertices to the original surface.
capabilities.outputs: clean low-poly mesh matching the source

capabilities.does: Dyntopo adds and removes triangles as the brush moves so detail follows the stroke. Detail types: Relative, Constant, Brush and Manual; refine methods: Subdivide Edges, Collapse Edges or both. Detail Flood Fill applies uniform detail across the whole object.
capabilities.inputs: mesh in Sculpt Mode; detail size

capabilities.does: Protects parts of a sculpt with a mask. Tools: box and lasso masks, invert, fill, clear, filters (smooth, sharpen, grow, shrink, contrast), mask from cavity, boundaries or colour, and random masks. Mask Extract and Mask Slice split masked geometry into new objects.
capabilities.inputs: mesh in Sculpt Mode; mask strokes
capabilities.outputs: masked regions; extracted or sliced meshes

capabilities.does: The manual lists 32 sculpt brush types, including Draw, Clay Strips, Inflate, Crease, Pinch, Grab, Elastic Deform, Snake Hook, Pose, Boundary, Cloth, Density, Draw Face Sets, Paint, Smear and Blur. Each type links to its own settings.
capabilities.inputs: mesh in Sculpt Mode; brush strokes

capabilities.does: Geometry Nodes builds and edits geometry from a node tree run by a modifier. Data-flow nodes change the geometry, function nodes compute values, and input nodes such as Position and ID feed them. Capture Attribute keeps a field's values after the geometry changes.

A field is a function evaluated per element in the context of the node it feeds, so one node tree gives a different value for each vertex or face. Field links are drawn dashed; linking a non-field socket into a field socket is an error.

Instance on Points creates instances that reference a geometry, object or collection without copying the data. Nested instancing works to eight levels for rendering. Realize Instances converts them to real geometry at a memory cost. Most nodes run once per unique geometry.
capabilities.inputs: points; geometry, object or collection to instance

capabilities.does: A Simulation Zone carries geometry from frame to frame: the Simulation Input starts from its inputs, later frames use the previous state, and Delta Time gives the step length. Results leave only through the Simulation Output. Frames cache during playback and can be baked.
capabilities.inputs: geometry and bake items; Delta Time

capabilities.does: The Bake node stores any part of a node tree, and simulation zones can be baked, so heavy results are not recomputed. One operator bakes all simulations and bake nodes of the selected objects. Volumes bake as OpenVDB. The blend-file must be saved first.
capabilities.inputs: node tree with bake nodes or simulation zones

capabilities.does: A Geometry Nodes group can run from menus as a one-shot tool instead of as a modifier. Group inputs appear in the Adjust Last Operation panel. The group declares supported modes and object types; tool-only nodes read the 3D cursor, mouse position and selection.
capabilities.inputs: node group set to Tool; current selection

capabilities.does: Cycles bakes shading into an image or colour attribute through the object's UV map. Bake types: Combined, Ambient Occlusion, Shadow, Position, Normal, UV, Roughness, Emit, Environment, Diffuse, Glossy, Transmission. Margin type Extend or Adjacent Faces pads UV islands.
capabilities.inputs: mesh with UVs; image texture node or colour attribute

capabilities.does: Selected to Active casts rays inward from the active low-poly object to the selected high-poly object, optionally through a cage object with set extrusion, or up to a maximum ray distance. Normal space can be tangent or object, with a swizzle per channel.
capabilities.inputs: high-poly and low-poly objects; cage; ray distance

capabilities.does: Turns selected faces into one or more UV islands in the UV Editor using a method chosen from the UV > Unwrap menu. Seams marked beforehand guide the cuts, and the method's settings sit in the Adjust Last Operation panel.

Texture Paint mode paints directly on an image applied to the mesh. The manual lists texture slots, brushes and brush assets, masks, symmetry, tiling, colour sampling, texture preview and a round trip through an external image editor.
capabilities.inputs: mesh with UVs and an image; brush strokes

capabilities.does: Principled BSDF is one shader node for most surfaces. Inputs: Base Color, Metallic, Roughness, IOR, Alpha, Normal; panels for Subsurface, Specular, Transmission, Coat, Sheen, Emission and Thin Film. Specular distribution is GGX or Multiscatter GGX.
capabilities.inputs: colour, roughness, metallic and panel values or textures

capabilities.does: The Noise Texture node generates fractal noise in 1D to 4D. Controls: scale, detail (octaves), roughness, lacunarity, offset, gain, distortion. Types: fBM, Multifractal, Hybrid Multifractal, Ridged Multifractal, Hetero Terrain. Outputs: a factor and a colour.
capabilities.inputs: vector or W coordinate; noise controls

capabilities.does: The Displacement node moves a surface along its normal using height, midlevel and scale, in object or world space. By default renders show bump mapping only; true displacement needs the material's displacement method changed and a finely subdivided mesh.
capabilities.outputs: displacement offset for the material output

capabilities.does: Cycles traces light paths per pixel. Settings: viewport and render sample counts, time limit, adaptive sampling by noise threshold, light tree, CPU path guiding for hard-to-reach lights, Automatic, Classic or Blue-Noise patterns, seeds, and rendering a subset of samples to split work.

Denoises Cycles output with OpenImageDenoise or OptiX, or picks automatically. The denoiser can use albedo and normal passes; OpenImageDenoise adds prefilter and quality levels. Denoising can run on the GPU for the viewport or the final render.
capabilities.inputs: noisy render plus optional albedo and normal passes

capabilities.does: Cycles renders on GPUs through CUDA and OptiX (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), oneAPI (Intel Arc) and Metal (Apple Silicon). OptiX, HIP, oneAPI and Metal use hardware ray tracing where the GPU has it. Scenes that exceed GPU memory can fall back to system memory.

EEVEE is a rasterizing render engine for interactive viewport work and final renders. It reads the same shader nodes as Cycles, so material previews carry over. The manual says it is less physically accurate than Cycles and keeps a separate limitations section.

Light objects are Point, Spot, Area and Sun. Common settings: colour or blackbody temperature, exposure, Normalize. Area lights take rectangle, square, disk or ellipse shapes; spot lights have cone angle and blend; point lights have radius and soft falloff.

The Sky Texture node makes a procedural sky. Multiple Scattering is the most accurate model; Single Scattering, Preetham and Hosek/Wilkie are marked legacy. Controls: sun elevation and rotation, sun size and intensity, altitude, air, aerosols, ozone.

Camera types: Perspective, Orthographic, Panoramic and Custom (OSL), the last two in Cycles only. Depth of field uses a focus object or distance, F-stop, blade count, blade rotation and ratio. Lens settings: focal length or field of view, shift, clip range, sensor fit.

Limits which objects a light illuminates and, with shadow linking, which objects block it. Objects join a linking collection as included or excluded. Cycles supports lights and emissive meshes; EEVEE supports lights only.
Freestyle is a line-based rendering system. Its manual section covers render settings, view-layer line sets and line styles, material settings and Python style modules, and lists known limitations.
capabilities.inputs: scene geometry; line set and line style

capabilities.does: View layers split a scene into separately rendered parts. The Passes section lists Data, Light, Cryptomatte, Shader AOV and Light Groups passes, with notes on combining passes and on EEVEE limits.

An armature object holds bones that deform attached geometry. Object Mode animates the whole armature, Pose Mode poses bones, Edit Mode sets the rest position. One armature data-block can serve several objects.

Positions the end bone of a chain and solves the other bones automatically. The Armature IK panel picks the Standard or iTaSC solver. Bone IK settings add per-axis lock, stiffness, limits and IK stretch; iTaSC adds damping, solver choice and simulation options.

Constraints tie an object or bone to a target or limit its transform. The manual groups them into Transform (Copy Location, Limit Rotation and others), Tracking (Track To, Damped Track, IK, Spline IK), Relationship (Child Of, Follow Path, Shrinkwrap, Armature) and Motion Tracking.

Rigify is a bundled add-on that generates a control rig from building-block rig types (Basic, Spines, Limbs, Faces, Skin) placed on a meta-rig. It supports custom meta-rigs, feature-set extensions and library linking.

Weight Paint mode edits vertex-group weights, used for bone deformation. The manual lists brushes, symmetry and editing operations such as Normalize, Mirror, Invert, Clean, Quantize, Smooth, Transfer Weights, Limit Total, Gradient and Locks.
capabilities.inputs: mesh with vertex groups; brush strokes

capabilities.does: Shape keys store alternative vertex positions of a mesh that can be blended. The manual covers relative and absolute shape keys, the Shape Keys panel and a workflow for adding vertices to a shaped mesh.

Drivers set a property from other values. The manual covers driver variables, scripted expressions and the Drivers editor, with examples such as transform drivers, a custom function and shape-key drivers; rotation values are in radians.

Keyframes store property values at frames with chosen interpolation and handle types. The manual covers inserting, deleting and clearing keyframes, keyframe types, and Keying Sets, including a whole-character set.
The Graph Editor shows animation as F-curves. The manual covers channels, curve editing and properties, and F-curve modifiers, plus the header, playback controls and sidebar.

The Dope Sheet edits keyframe timing. Its modes are Action Editor, Shape Key Editor, Grease Pencil and Mask; menus cover select, marker, channel and key operations, with snapping and proportional editing.

The Nonlinear Animation editor arranges actions as strips on tracks. Strip types are Action, Transition, Sound and Meta. It has track and strip editing and a sidebar for the edited action, strip and modifiers.

Shows where points such as object origins and bone joints travel over a frame range, red for past and green for future. Options: Around Frame or In Range, calculation range, step, bake to the active camera, bake location, frame numbers and keyframe markers.
capabilities.inputs: selected objects or bones; frame range

capabilities.does: Mesh objects become active or passive rigid bodies. The simulation overrides position and orientation without changing stored values, and Apply Object Transform bakes the result. The manual also covers rigid body constraints, the rigid body world, cache and field weights.
capabilities.inputs: mesh objects; mass and collision settings

capabilities.does: Cloth is simulated with virtual springs between mesh vertices: tension, compression, shear and angular bending, each adjustable. Deflection objects, wind and other forces act on it. Frames are cached.

Fluid physics needs a Domain object and at least one Flow object, with optional Effectors. It covers liquids and gas (smoke and fire), baked to a cache. Quick Liquid and Quick Smoke create a domain with basic settings.
Soft Body simulates deformable objects. The manual's settings cover Goal, Edges, Self Collision, Solver and Cache, with interior and exterior forces and collision with other objects.

The particle system has Emitter and Hair types. Emitter settings cover emission, velocity, rotation, physics, render and viewport display, children, force fields and vertex groups. Hair adds hair dynamics and shape. Particle Edit Mode edits the result.
Force field objects act on simulations. Types: Force, Wind, Vortex, Magnetic, Harmonic, Charge, Lennard-Jones, Texture, Curve Guide, Boid, Turbulence, Drag and Fluid Flow.

Curves sculpt mode grooms hair curves with brushes: Add, Delete, Density, Comb, Snake Hook, Grow/Shrink, Pinch, Puff, Smooth, Slide and Selection Paint, with shared brush, stroke, falloff and cursor settings.

Grease Pencil objects store strokes drawn with a mouse or pen in 3D space, for 2D animation, cut-outs, motion graphics and storyboards. Strokes are drawn in Draw Mode and adjusted in Edit and Sculpt modes; materials, modifiers, lighting and effects apply.
capabilities.inputs: pen or mouse strokes on keyframes

capabilities.does: The compositor combines renders and images with nodes: input, output, colour, filter, keying, mask, transform (including Displace and Lens Distortion), tracking, camera and lens effects, texture, creative and utility nodes, plus node groups.

The Video Sequencer arranges and overlays clips, adds fades and transitions, and syncs audio. Strip types in the manual include Movie, Sound, Text, Glow, Cross and Wipe. Listed workflows are montage editing and storyboarding.

The Movie Clip editor tracks markers, solves camera and object motion, supports plane tracks and 2D stabilization, and reconstructs the scene. Manual lens calibration and tools for scene orientation are listed.

Scripts use bpy.data for data-blocks, bpy.context (read-only) for the current state, and bpy.ops to run operators. Scripts add operators, panels and menus by subclassing bpy.types classes; custom properties save with the file and can be animated.

Imports and exports baked animated geometry. Export options: frame range, sub-frame sampling, instancing, flatten hierarchy, UVs, normals, colour attributes, face sets, subdivision schema, triangulate, hair as curves and particles as points. Import can set the frame range and read split sequences.

Imports and exports USD scenes: usd and usdz files, hierarchy, animation, cameras, lights, meshes, curves, volumes, points, shape keys and armatures. Materials map to and from USD Preview Surface, with MaterialX export and texture options.
capabilities.outputs: USD or USDZ file, or imported scene

capabilities.does: The bundled glTF 2.0 add-on writes .glb or .gltf with meshes, Principled BSDF materials, textures, cameras, punctual lights and keyframe, shape key and skinning animation. Options include Draco and Meshopt compression and animation modes.

FBX import reads custom normals, subdivision data, vertex colours, armatures with an option to drop leaf bones, and each take as a separate action. Export goes through the FBX add-on, documented on a separate page.

Volume objects hold grids loaded from OpenVDB files. The manual lists grid and file properties, viewport display and render settings, and notes rendering and limitations. Geometry Nodes bakes volumes as OpenVDB.

scripting: Python API (bpy: data, context, ops, types, msgbus)

Six style node groups show a structure as Ball and Stick, Cartoon, Ribbon, Spheres, Sticks or Surface. Cartoon highlights helices and sheets and can compute secondary structure; Ball and Stick can estimate bonds by distance when the file has none.

capabilities.does: Style Surface computes a molecular surface from van der Waals radii and a probe, approximating other surface algorithms, and by default colours each point by its nearest alpha carbon. Relax, offset and fillet inputs shape it.
Since version 520.0.0 the spheres style uses instance-based spheres under EEVEE and point-based spheres under Cycles.

About 30 selection node groups pick atoms by element, residue name or ID range, backbone, side chain, helix, sheet, loop, lipid, solvent, hydrogen, bonded depth, distance from target atoms, or a sphere or cube object. Results combine with And and Or inputs.

Colour node groups set colours by atomic number, element, residue name, secondary structure, rainbow along chains, an attribute map, and the AlphaFold pLDDT palette from the b_factor attribute. A Goodsell mode darkens non-carbon atoms; mixing works in OKLab.
Animate Frames plays a structure's trajectory frames onto its atoms with optional smoothing and interpolation. Animate Trails adds trails that follow atoms for a set number of frames behind.

Animate Peptide to Curve aligns a protein's residues along an input curve, with offset, start, end, rotate and twist inputs.

Builds an elastic network by linking atoms within a cutoff distance, then simulates it in Geometry Nodes with substeps, force, drag and particle radius. Other nodes simulate curves and motion on faces, with Brownian, gravity and mesh-collision forces.

Three density style nodes render electron microscopy volumes: ISO Surface (threshold, contours, positive and negative colours), Surface, and Wire (with wire radius and resolution). Hide Dust removes small stray regions.
DNA nodes handle oxDNA models: oxDNA Style Ribbon draws backbone and bases, helper nodes recover and realize the vectors, and DNA From Curve builds DNA along a curve.

Ensemble nodes instance the items of an ensemble onto points, place assembly instances, and read rotations from RELION and cisTEM star files. Periodic nodes replicate a trajectory across box boundaries.
Periodic Box, Periodic Image, Periodic Array and Lattice Grid nodes read box vectors from a trajectory and replicate the geometry across periodic boundaries.

A Python package exposes add_style() for building style nodes, a SelectionManager for named selections, a Canvas for scene setup and a framing module for camera fitting; node groups are also available as typed Python classes.

scripting: Python API (molecularnodes package, add_style, SelectionManager, Canvas)

engines.name: PyMeshLab filter set
engines.does: Python bindings call the same filters by identifier through apply_filter().

capabilities.does: Edits, cleans, repairs and inspects triangle meshes; the site lists automatic mesh optimization and noise removal among highlights.

The Close Holes filter (meshing_close_holes) fills holes whose boundary has fewer edges than maxholesize (default 30). Further options cover selected-only holes, self-intersection checks and refining the new triangles.

Quadric Edge Collapse Decimation with Texture (meshing_decimation_quadric_edge_collapse_with_texture) simplifies a textured mesh while keeping its UV layout. It takes a target face count or percentage, a quality threshold and boundary and normal preservation switches.

Three reconstruction filters build surfaces from points: Ball Pivoting rolls a ball over an oriented point cloud, Screened Poisson makes watertight surfaces from oriented points, and VCG reconstructs volumetrically from all visible layers.
ICP Between Meshes aligns a source mesh to a reference mesh by iterative closest point; Global Align Meshes aligns a set of meshes together.
Smoothing filters include Laplacian, Taubin, HC Laplacian and a feature-preserving TwoStep method; Depth Smooth smooths only along a viewing direction.
Computes principal curvature directions per vertex and colours vertices by RIMLS curvature.
Parametrization filters: Trivial Per-Triangle, Flat Plane, Harmonic, Least Squares Conformal Maps, and parametrization from registered rasters. Iso Parametrization builds an atlased mesh.
Texture Map Defragmentation merges texture atlas charts to reduce fragmentation, using matching, boundary and distortion tolerances.
Compute Ambient occlusion shoots rays from face barycentres; a second filter computes per-vertex or per-face occlusion from many view directions, optionally on the GPU.
Transfers per-vertex colour into a texture image.
Convex Hull computes the convex hull of the input with Qhull.
Estimates vertex normals for point sets without face connectivity, and smooths normals on point sets.
Fractal Displacement adds terrain-like perturbation with octave, lacunarity and seed settings; Random Vertex Displacement and Cubic stylization are other geometry filters.
PyMeshLab runs filters from Python through apply_filter(), using filter identifiers and named parameters.

outcomes: Textured meshes prepared for 3D printing or display

capabilities.does: Pushes selected polygon faces out as new geometry, together or one at a time, in local or world space. Settings include divisions, offset, thickness, taper, twist, and gravity or magnet pull.
Replaces selected edges with new faces. Controls are offset (width), depth, segments, roundness with auto-fit, chamfer, mitering and angle, smoothing angle, and a rule for UVs on the new faces.

Builds a new mesh from union, difference or intersection of input meshes. Optional thresholds merge near vertices and collapse tiny faces first; it can tag the intersection and merge UV sets by name or by link.

Setting the Boolean node geometry mode to Volume converts inputs to voxels, computes union, difference or intersection there, and returns polygons. Voxel size controls detail; the default is 1.0 and very small values trigger a heavy-geometry warning.
Copies a mesh across a chosen axis and plane, then merges the shared border to give a symmetric result. Merge mode and threshold, pivot and world or object space are adjustable.

Smooths a mesh or selected faces by subdividing recursively. Parameters: divisions, continuity from 0 (subdivide only) to 1, border and hard-edge keeping, UV smoothing, and a choice between Maya subdivision and OpenSubdiv Catmull-Clark.

Reduces polygon count while keeping the overall shape. The newer algorithm can target a percentage, vertex count or triangle count and can preserve borders, hard edges, crease edges, topology type and quads.
capabilities.inputs: polygon mesh, target count or percent

capabilities.does: Triangulates a mesh, then splits edges longer than a maximum length and collapses edges below a threshold given as a share of that length. A smoothing strength relaxes vertices afterwards.
Flow Retopology 1.3 is bundled with Maya 2026. For complex geometry it moves the processing of retopology jobs to the cloud.

Creates a lattice deformer around selected objects; moving lattice points reshapes enclosed geometry. Divisions set the slice count, a flag fits the lattice to the object, and outside-lattice mode controls points beyond the base volume.

Loft builds a NURBS surface through two or more curves. Options: degree, section spans, closing into a periodic surface, uniform parameterization, per-curve reverse and cusp, and polygon or subdivision-surface output.
Auto projection creates UVs by projecting the surface onto 4, 5, 6, 8 or 12 planes. Options include optimising face assignment, two-direction projection, scale mode and a named UV set.
Lays out UV pieces so they do not overlap. Controls: layout in a U row or square, block or shape stacking, scale mode, cut mode, rotation for best fit, and padding up to 5 percent.

Transfers surface detail from source meshes onto a target mesh as a map. Output types: normal, displacement, diffuse RGB, lit-and-shaded RGB, alpha. Settings: map size, file format, search cage, tangent or object space, supersampling.

Sets keys on attributes at a time and value. Options include in and out tangent types (such as clamped, linear, step), insert without changing curve shape, breakdown keys, and placing keys in an animation layer or clip.

Replaces whatever drives an attribute (constraints, simulation, expressions) with plain animation curves sampled over a time range at a chosen step. Can evaluate the whole scene per step, which dynamics need.
Time Editor clips sit on tracks and are created from an animation source, moved and removed by command. Two clips on a track blend with a crossfade mode, and clip blend mode is normal or additive.
The shot command makes shot nodes for the Camera Sequencer. Each shot has a time range on the Maya timeline, a separate range in the sequence, a camera, an image-plane clip, audio and a track.
The Graph Editor gained Channel Sets, which group channels so animators can share the groups, and a View menu option that shows or hides pins.

Creates IK handles over a joint chain. Solver choices are rotate-plane, single-chain and spline; settings include priority, weight, stickiness, spline curve and span count, and switching a handle between IK and FK.

Binds geometry to joints with smooth skinning. Bind methods: closest distance, closest in hierarchy, heat map, geodesic voxel. Skin methods: classical linear, dual quaternion, blend. Also max influences, weight normalisation, add or remove influence.
Blends weighted target shapes into a base mesh. Targets are indexed with weights; in-between shapes, envelope scale, topology check, and placement in the deformer chain are options.

A parent constraint makes an object follow the position and rotation of one or more targets by weight. It can keep the starting offset, skip chosen axes, work on an animation layer, and cache results to avoid flips.
Per-vertex analysis tools that help improve character deformation, drive effects such as animated wrinkles, and find problem areas in rigs. New in the 2026.3 update.
MotionMaker is an animation tool in Maya for producing character movement quickly; the page says it needs no outside motion-capture gear and no other application, and gives no further detail.

nParticle makes particle objects from world-space points. Per-particle attributes can be queried and edited by ID or index; settings include momentum conservation, inherited emitter velocity, grid spacing, and caching.

The fluid emitter adds density, heat or fuel to fluid objects. Types are omni point, directional point, surface and curve; separate rates, a dropoff, and volume shapes (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) shape the emission.

Bifrost 2.13 runs a FLIP liquid solver inside the node graph with adaptive resolution, particle foam, colored liquid emitted from source color sets, influences for refinement, and .bob file caching. It is close to the older Bifrost Fluids plug-in.
Bifrost 2.15 adds first rigid-body dynamics to the graph, plus fracturing and boolean modeling operations, in the Maya 2026.3 update.

The Bifrost Graph Editor builds procedural effects from nodes. The Bifrost Browser (Windows menu) holds sample graphs by category that can be imported, with their lights, input geometry and animation.

MASH builds a network from a Waiter hub, a Distribute node and a geometry node (Repro or Instancer). Repros are full copies and more versatile; instances are faster. Extra nodes stack to change the result.

XGen Interactive Groom Editor: add modifiers to a description, stack sculpt layers with weights and keys, merge layers, transfer a groom to another mesh even with different topology, and save presets.
The XGen Description menu can write hair to Alembic cache files for later loading.
USD for Maya 0.34 adds an Asset Resolver for loading assets and moving projects. Version 0.32 exports animation curves for camera attributes.
OpenPBR is the default surface shader in Maya 2026, and LookdevX 1.8 adds OpenPBR support to FBX export.
Substance for Maya (3.0.4 in Maya 2026) loads Substance materials in the scene.
Arnold for Maya ships with Maya (5.5.2 to 5.5.4 across 2026 updates). Updates list faster scene start-up, USD improvements, an Inference imager, and better global light sampling.
Golaem, a crowd simulation and character layout plug-in, joined the Media and Entertainment Collection and is introduced in the Maya 2026 notes.
Maya 2026 supports WebM for playblast export, image planes and the Camera Sequencer.
A unit-conversion dialog appears on STL import and export, because STL files carry no units; the user picks the units for conversion.

Python API 2.0 (OpenMaya) gives function sets such as MFnDependencyNode to create nodes, find plugs and connections, add attributes and read UUIDs. Developer help also lists Python API 1.0, mayapy, PyMEL and the Python command reference.
The C++ API supports command plug-ins and dependency graph plug-ins; the developer help also lists the Viewport 2.0 API, a .NET API and a UFE API reference.
MEL, Maya's own scripting language, has a scripting guide and a command reference in the developer help.

scripting: Bifrost graph scripting (docs list a Bifrost scripting section)

rea.notes: Closed source. Public: Python and MEL command references, Python API 2.0 reference, C++ API reference, What's New pages. EULA not opened. Autodesk product page returned 403 to the fetch tool.

entries.name: Autodesk 3ds Max

licence.name: commercial subscription (plan terms not read; Autodesk product pages return 403 to the fetch tool)

engines.name: Particle Flow
engines.does: Event-driven particle system built from operators and tests wired into events inside the Particle View dialog.

engines.name: MassFX
engines.does: Rigid body, constraint, ragdoll and mCloth physics with a toolbar, a tools dialog, an Explorer, a Visualizer and baking to keyframes.

engines.name: Cloth and Garment Maker modifiers
engines.does: Cloth simulation against collision objects and forces, and stitching of 2D spline patterns into 3D garments.

engines.name: Max Creation Graph
engines.does: Visual node editor for building new tools such as modifiers and controllers that then appear in the Create panel.

engines.name: Biped, Physique and Crowd (character studio)
engines.does: Footstep-driven biped animation, skinning with Physique, and crowd animation.

engines.name: CAT
engines.does: Character Animation Toolkit: CATRig rigging, layered nonlinear animation, mocap import and muscle objects.

engines.name: Arnold for 3ds Max (MAXtoA)
engines.does: Arnold renderer integration; the 2026 updates list a 5.8.2.0 and a 5.8.3.2 release.

capabilities.does: TurboSmooth subdivides a whole object to round corners, producing a NURMS object. Settings: viewport iterations 0 to 10, separate render iterations, isoline display, explicit normals, smoothing by material ID or smoothing group.

The Cloth modifier simulates cloth against collision objects and forces such as gravity and wind. It defines cloth and collision objects, makes constraints, lets you drag cloth, and erases parts of the simulation.

The Garment Maker modifier turns 2D spline patterns into 3D garments: convert a pattern to a mesh, arrange panels, create seams, and mark internal seam lines for creases and cuts. It can import patterns from other applications.

The Skin modifier deforms a mesh with bones using envelopes, cross sections and vertex weights. Tools: weight solver, weight table, weight tool, paint weights with blending, rigid vertices, normalise, exclude vertices, and bake selected vertices.
A toggle on the Skin modifier mixes linear and dual-quaternion deformation to reduce volume loss when limbs twist. Blend-weight editing can target the dual-quaternion mask.
The Attribute Transfer modifier moves several kinds of attributes between objects. It arrived in the 2026.1 update.
The Conform modifier projects one object onto another; the 2026.3 update adds a distance parameter to its Shrink Wrap projection method.
The 3ds Max 2026.1 update reduces the default value of the Vertex Weld modifier to 0.001.
Edit Poly Chamfer cuts off selected edges, making new edges and polygons. It can be dragged interactively or set with Chamfer Amount, an Open option and segments.
Edit Poly Connect adds new edges between pairs of selected edges on the same polygon. Settings: number of segments, spacing and placement. New edges do not cross.
Edit Poly Extrude pushes selected edges out: vertical drag sets height and horizontal drag sets base width. Extrude Settings opens a caddy with a numeric Extrusion Height.
Edit Poly Bridge joins two border edges with a connecting polygon in a straight line, with a settings caddy for interactive bridging.
Create Shape From Selection turns selected edges into a spline. A dialog sets the shape name and whether the result is smooth or linear.

Optimize Spline reduces knots on a spline. The 2026.1 update adds a Colinear Knots method that drops knots on a straight line, animatable By Percentage and By Maximum values, and corner-type changes that avoid self-intersecting loops.

Unwrap UVW provides Flatten Mapping (planar maps on contiguous polygons within an angle), Normal Mapping (planar maps by vector projection), Unfold Mapping, and Spline Map dialogs to build UV clusters.
Pelt Map flattens a complex UV map with a virtual stretcher and springs. Controls: Start Pelt, simulation samples, pull strength, stiffness, dampening, decay, mirror stretcher, and lock open edges.
The Pack dialog rearranges texture clusters procedurally inside the Edit UVWs editor.
The Relax Tool dialog adjusts spacing of selected texture vertices by parameters to reduce or remove distortion; Pelt also has a Start Relax button.
Render UVs exports the texture mapping as a bitmap template. You paint over it in a 2D program and reapply the bitmap in 3ds Max.

MassFX makes rigid bodies and constraints the base of a physics simulation. Bodies are Dynamic (affect and are affected) or Kinematic (affect but are not affected). Ragdolls take part as rigid bodies.
mCloth is a Cloth modifier variant that collides with, and is moved by, other MassFX objects in the same simulation.
Baking converts MassFX simulation results into ordinary keyframed animation and turns Dynamic objects into Kinematic ones. The MassFX Visualizer helps check hard-to-spot problems.
Rigid bodies, constraints and ragdolls from MassFX can be exported for use in games or other real-time simulation.

Particle Flow builds particle systems from events that hold operators (such as Birth, Shape, Speed) and tests that send particles to other events. Particle View has a depot, event display and parameters panel.

Max Creation Graph creates tools (modifiers, controllers, geometry) from nodes. Example workflow: add a primitive node, generate tool inputs, connect to an Output: Geometry node, save, evaluate, then use the tool from the Create panel.
capabilities.outputs: new modifier, controller or geometry tool

capabilities.does: MAXScript is the built-in scripting language; the 2026 notes list items such as the menu system, color management, UserGridSettings, createDialog, and List Controllers.

pymxs is the supported Python route into 3ds Max: it runs MAXScript from Python, handles by-reference parameters, and exposes custom attributes. Python 3 is bundled with venv support; a qtmax helper module covers Qt widgets.
USD for 3ds Max 0.13, shipped with the 2026.3 update, adds an Asset Resolver and lets users duplicate, rename, delete and reparent prims.
OpenPBR materials load and display faster in the viewport when they do not use SSS, Coat, Fuzz or ThinFilm (2026.1 update note).

The Slate Material Editor keeps a separate thumbnail per color-management setting, so changing view transform does not force re-rendering; a preference can stop sample swatches re-rendering. Material Switcher index can be animated.

Arnold for 3ds Max is integrated as the bundled renderer (5.8.2.0 and 5.8.3.2 in 2026 updates); notes list faster scene start, USD improvements, an Inference imager, faster global light sampling and GPU volumes.
CAT builds characters on the CATRig hierarchy without scripting, with an FK and IK rig manipulation system to push and pull parts into pose.
CATMotion generates walk and motion cycles that match rig velocity and direction, with footprint collision detection to avoid sliding feet, even on uneven ground.
CAT animation layering applies edits non-destructively; layers and stacks can be saved and reused on other characters. The Layer Manager loads mocap and keyframe data.
CAT loads and edits motion-capture data with the same tools as keyframes: import, mapping, retargeting and editing; keyframe tools transform, duplicate and retime motion.
Biped animation can be driven by footsteps or freeform keys, and converted between types. Dynamics and spline dynamics, In Place mode, Motion Flow and the Transition Editor support the workflow.
The Motion Mixer mixes animations on a Biped, and Motion Flow combines them using the Transition Editor.
CAT muscle objects are non-rendering helpers that drive realistic skin stretch and deformation.
The Crowd system in character studio animates groups of characters; the workflow guide lists crowd cognitive controllers.

scripting: C++ SDK (developer help exists; not read in detail)
outcomes: rendered stills and sequences with Arnold

rea.notes: Closed source. Public: help, MAXScript reference, Python and Max Creation Graph developer help. EULA not opened. Some pages cited are from older help editions (2015 to 2024); behaviour may differ in 2026.

entries.name: Autodesk Mudbox

licence.name: commercial subscription; end of sale announced (3-year plans ended 2026-08-07, 1-year and monthly end 2026-11-07)

engines.name: Gigatexel Engine
engines.does: Lets you paint on lower-resolution proxy images while strokes are stored in the full-resolution texture; tiles near the camera load automatically.

engines.name: Retopologize
engines.does: Builds new quad topology from a sculpted mesh, optionally guided by curves, and transfers sculpt layers, paint layers and posing data.

capabilities.does: Brush-based sculpting works across subdivision levels, with 3D layers for sculpt edits; the About page lists Subdivision Levels and 3D Layers among its core features.
Stamps are images that mask a sculpt tool tip: black protects the model and white lets the tool act. A stamp can repeat along the stroke, or the Imprint tool places a single instance.
capabilities.outputs: surface detail such as scales or stitching

capabilities.does: A stencil image is placed in the 3D view, scaled, rotated or tiled, then a sculpt tool is stroked across it to transfer its detail. Mirror, flip, visibility, strength and a Use Tiles option adjust the result.
The About page lists tangent-based symmetry sculpting among the core features.

The Retopologize window sets a target base face count, a uniformity slider (even faces versus faithful shape), curve guides (soft and hard constraint), symmetry options, and which data transfers to the new mesh.
Paint on a model in 3D Paint mode with the Paint Brush tool; strokes land on paint layers, which hold 2D bitmaps and let you separate paint between layers. Stamps can paint decals or tattoos.
Stencil Projection projects color from a 2D stencil image positioned in the 3D View onto the model.
The Gigatexel Engine handles large texture sets by painting on proxies and writing strokes to the full-resolution texture. Preferences set paint buffer memory, and a hotkey forces texture sync.
Ptex painting maps every base face of the mesh with its own texture, so no UV layout is needed.
UVs & Maps > Create UVs makes a quick set of rough UVs inside Mudbox; the UV View shows whether a model has UVs and how paint fits them.

outcomes: normal and displacement maps for other DCC tools

entries.name: Modo

licence.name: commercial; development ended after 17.1; existing customers can get an extended 10-year licence

engines.name: mPath
engines.does: Modo renderer redesigned from the ground up: hybrid CPU and GPU, per-light outputs in one render, OptiX, CUDA and Metal GPU paths, Embree on CPU.

engines.name: MeshFusion
engines.does: Procedural assemblies that fuse simple geometry into complex models with trims, profile sweeps and slicers.

engines.name: Replicators
engines.does: Procedural duplication of items on surfaces or particles; 16.1 adds a Particle Clone operator for editing single clones.

capabilities.does: mPath is Modo's renderer, redesigned for faster ray tracing, more accurate Fresnel and refraction, and hybrid CPU/GPU compute with fewer controls.
Render Outputs Per Light uses light path expressions: Render > Add Per-Light Render Outputs creates an LPE output per light, selectable in the Render window Output list.

GPU options: NVIDIA OptiX for ray tracing, CUDA for shading, and Metal for ray tracing on macOS; Intel Embree handles CPU ray tracing. Multiple GPUs are not supported, and several features are unsupported on GPU.
mPath QuickCam (Alt+F9) renders interactively while you pan, dolly and rotate the camera and change light intensity or camera settings.
Denoising is supported, with a Denoise Per Iteration option for per-light render outputs.

When an HDR image, or any other active texture layer, lights the environment, the mPath renderer turns on environment importance sampling by itself. The NVIDIA CUDA shading engine does not support that sampling.

MeshFusion builds models with subtractive trims on a Fusion Item. Assemblies include Fusion Damage Trim, Fusion Slicer 3Point and 7Point, Profile Sweep and RibTrim; Fusion-Ready Presets swap profiles.
The ElboPipe assembly builds piping from straight segments and short bends with optional elbow joints; Pen Extrude makes its curves from a polyline path.
Modo 16.1 adds MeshFusion Geodesic Strips, which make MeshFusion more reliable and easier to troubleshoot.
Surface Strip Embossing (Modo 14.0) creates embossed strips on Fusion Items from curves (simple, Bezier, B-Spline) or from text.

Planar Decal places images on surfaces with low distortion without UV editing; Seam Decals draw an image-based seam along a curve; Surface Probe projects floating decals and bakes them into the receiving surface.
Mesh Paint (and Mesh Paint Replica) places meshes onto another mesh surface, with an Edit Mode to reposition and reorient the placed items.
Replicators duplicate items procedurally; the Particle Clone operator in 16.1 makes cloned items individually editable.
Triplanar projection blends textures projected from several directions, so materials can be applied without UVs.
Edge Chamfer supports profile presets (a 1D shape defining the chamfer), reverse direction, reverse depth and falloffs.
Unbevel collapses beveled faces between two selected edge loops.
Unwrap & Relax combines the Unwrap tool and UV Relax in one step to create a UV pelt.
UV Relax has an Ignore Edge Selection option so currently selected edges are not considered when relaxing.

The Enhanced Bezier tool adds Illustrator-style shortcuts, surface-aligned handles and tangent controls. Curve booleans let open curves trim geometry and self-intersecting closed curves become single shapes.
The Background Constraint Target Item constrains retopology to one chosen item while the rest of the scene stays visible.
Modo 14.0 lets mesh operations create vertex maps and fill them procedurally with weights, edge weights, seams and RGB values; a further operation selects elements by vertex map value.
Falloffs (Linear, Cylinder, Radial, Noise, Path, Lasso, Image) gained a Use World Transforms option that treats all selected surfaces as one.
Viewport Curvature Shading lightens convex and darkens concave areas to read forms more easily; viewport transparency quality and speed were also improved.
mPath can render AxF materials, per the 14.0 notes.

rea.notes: Closed source. Foundry ended development after Modo 17.1 (announced 2024-11-07); docs and downloads promised to at least 2025-11 and may be retired. Features cited come from versions 14.0 to 16.1 notes.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, Foundry end-of-life page and Learn help pages read

licence.name: commercial; new licence listed at GBP 795 by press, plan type (perpetual or subscription) not stated

engines.name: Modeler
engines.does: Modelling application that holds the bevel, fillet, Surface Wrap and UV tools.

engines.name: Layout
engines.does: Scene application with Advanced Placement, tracking and effects plug-ins.

engines.name: RiPR / RiPR 2
engines.does: Path-traced viewport preview in Layout; 2 adds mesh lighting, tangent-space normal maps and temporal denoise.

engines.name: OctaneRender for LightWave
engines.does: Bundled GPU renderer; the 2026 version adds Gaussian Splat preview, meshlets and OCIO light support.

capabilities.does: Advanced Bevel extends the standard bevel with a Bezier curve editor for the bevel profile.
The Fillet tool rounds corners on planar geometry.
Surface Wrap wraps an object around a target surface, such as a label on a bottle.
UV Serpent, a Modeler plug-in, generates UV maps for curved polygon strips such as pipes, roads or ropes.
Atlas UV is an updated atlas mapping function that keeps UV island scale and packs islands more tightly than the legacy system.
Advanced Placement scatters objects in real time with physics: they settle under gravity, and can shatter on contact with the ground.
RiPR is a path-traced viewport preview in Layout; results can render in real time or be baked for offline rendering. RiPR 2 adds mesh-based lighting and tangent-space normal mapping.
RiPR 2 uses temporal denoising through NVIDIA OptiX.

MotoRig semi-automatically rigs vehicles from parameters such as mass, weight distribution and banking; it covers terrain following to full suspension dynamics with six shock absorber presets, for four-wheel and larger military vehicles.
The Fracture tool pre-fractures geometry for destruction simulation, keeps materials and UVs, and offers several shard distribution patterns; it runs in real time on simpler meshes.
THOR is an object replacement plug-in that makes procedural lightning as 3D geometry with thickness and heat weight maps, forked or recursive branching, and animatable parameters.
Snow Falling 3D is a mesh deformer plug-in for snow and rain inside a volume or the camera view; it instances meshes or VDBs and has gravity, wind, updrift and turbulence effectors with motion blur.

Ocean Spectrum Controller animates water surfaces with three spectral types (including classic Tessendorf), a micro bump shader, and weight maps for wind direction, depth, falloff and attaching to boats.
A parallax shader makes a 2D window texture look like a 3D interior, using a Window node, in the native renderer and in OctaneRender.
The Ivy generator grows climbing plants across surfaces, with gravity, surface adhesion and randomness controls.
The 3D Camera Tracker in Layout uses the open-source COLMAP pipeline to reconstruct real camera motion into an animated camera; it can also output sparse or dense point clouds or meshes.
The Motion Pixel Tracker follows features in background image sequences and creates animated nulls that follow them.
A built-in browser for 3D models, images, videos, HDRIs and IES data, with Quixel Megascans and Maxtree library integration.
OctaneRender for LightWave is bundled; the 2026 build adds 3D Gaussian Splatting (previewable in Layout), meshlets, virtual textures, OCIO for lights and more gradient nodes.
SpiderWeb generates cobwebs as real 3D geometry, with chaotic and spiral options.

rea.notes: Closed source. Vendor home page lists a 2026 documentation link that was not opened; capabilities come from CG Channel coverage of the LightWave 2026 release (2026-06-15). LightWave Digital acquired the software from Vizrt in 2023 per the same article.

engines.name: Particle Bind solver

Simulates granular materials such as sand.
Rigid body dynamics and destruction through the PhysX solver, which needs a CUDA-capable Nvidia GPU.
Soft body simulation; tyFlex is offered as an alternative to the native 3ds Max Flex modifier.
Cloth simulation backed by a Cloth Collision Solver that needs a CUDA-capable Nvidia GPU.
Particle-driven crowd animation using the tyActor object.
Imports and manipulates OpenVDB data so volumes can interact with particle systems.
tyCache is the Pro caching system; 1.007 added sub-frame memory caching for more precise simulation retiming.
Birth Fluid and Fluid Force operators (1.007) generate and move whitewater such as foam, spray and bubbles during liquid simulation.
The Grow operator generates procedural vegetation across surfaces using an ivy algorithm (added 1.010, updated 1.012) with intersection controls.

Release 1.012 adds 20 terrain operators: an erosion solver, layered surface colouring with flow maps, mesh-to-terrain conversion, interactive sculpting against imported meshes, a shallow water solver, and rock scattering.

engines.name: Dyverso

engines.name: RealWave

capabilities.does: Hybrido2 is the HyFLIP-based liquid solver aimed at big scenes; the vendor page names floods and breaking ocean waves as examples.
Dyverso is a multiphysics solver that handles liquid, granular, rigid and elastic materials in one setup.
RealWave builds small to medium ocean surfaces.
Caronte is the built-in rigid and soft body dynamics solver.
Hybrido Secondary Fluids form their own node family; the reference gives splash, foam and bubbles as examples.
Mesh nodes turn particles or Hybrido data into surfaces: Particle Meshes (RK and OpenVDB, plus legacy) and Hybrido Meshes (Basic and OpenVDB).
The node reference lists Objects and MultiBodies, MultiJoints and MultiServos for jointed mechanical setups.
Free connectivity plug-ins export simulations to host 3D platforms; product pages are listed for Cinema 4D, Maya and 3ds Max.
RealFlow's node pipeline can send different iterations of a scene, or secondary Hybrido elements, to a farm for calculation to save time. The page names no farm software.

engines.name: Liquid simulator
engines.does: Liquid simulation with splashes and foam inside 3ds Max and Maya.

engines.name: Fire and smoke simulator
engines.does: Adaptive-grid dynamics engine for fire and smoke.

engines.name: Procedural ocean

capabilities.does: Liquids with splashes and foam are simulated in the host application; foam is faster and more varied in pattern size and look.
Fire and smoke come from an adaptive-grid dynamics engine, driven also by expressions.
Ocean surfaces do not repeat and use procedural displacement, so they preview and render without simulating cache files; they can transition into simulated beach waves.
Emission can come from animated meshes, texture maps and particles.
Wind, spline-follow and mesh-attraction forces steer simulations, and Massive Wave Force builds ocean simulations.
The Phoenix shader renders liquids and volumetric effects; the vendor page names V-Ray and Corona as renderers.
Compatibility is stated for OpenVDB and Alembic data.
The vendor page lists rigid body simulation among Phoenix simulation types.

The Population Tool places a locator and creates a particle system linked to a Crowd Field, which instantiates characters on the particles; simulation runs when the timeline plays.
A Terrain Locator (an infinite plane by default) lets characters' feet adapt to the ground.
In the Behavior Editor you add a Motion Behavior to an Entity Type and choose a motion; Visual Feedback shows which behaviors run.
In the Character Maker Geometry tab, Rendering Types sliders set mesh weights to vary geometry across a crowd.
The Simulation Exporter writes a cache with chosen name, frame range and folder, creates a CacheProxy and switches to Cache Replay mode for scrubbing and rendering.
The Simulation Cache Layout tool adds non-destructive deformation layers to a cache and saves them in a Layout File (.gscl) while exported files stay unchanged.
The documentation index lists Golaem for Maya, 3ds Max, Houdini, Katana, Unreal and USD, plus Golaem Layout.

capabilities.does: A node-based interface builds AI-driven agents without programming. Brain parts are reusable logic; the Parts Library has over 40 prebuilt parts such as collision avoidance, formations and lane following.
An Action Page stores agent actions (mocap clips or keyframes); a Motion Page designs motion as one or more motion trees; a blending engine moves the brain between actions.
Massive Prime authors, directs and renders custom autonomous agents for animation and VFX; Smart Stunts let agents perform mocap or keyframed actions while colliding with others and the environment.
Cloth tools make cloth from arbitrary geometry for robes, cloaks and flags, with a solver meant to run on thousands of agents.
Rigid Body Dynamics and Bullet dynamics handle falling bodies, accessories and projectiles.
Dynamic hair and fur simulation for agents.
A patented Vision system lets agents perceive their surroundings each frame, and hearing also feeds into agent brains.
A Python API scripts agent actions, placement and motion import; Massive for Maya also has a MEL API for tasks such as scripted placement.
Agents render through 3Delight, Air, RenderMan, Mental Ray, V-Ray and Arnold (sold separately); Massive for Maya batch renders with those renderers need no license.

Massive for Maya places terrain, agent groups, placement generators, lanes and flow fields in Maya's Outliner and Attribute Editor; a record button and shelf status indicator run and play back simulations. A Maya import dialog brings lights, cameras, skeletons and motion into Massive Prime.

Ready To Run Agents are prebuilt agents with skeletons, motion libraries, brains, geometry, textures and shaders, sold separately; the site lists Ambient, Stadium, Mayhem, Combat Sword, Horse and Rider, Locomotion and Car agents.

entries.name: Cinema 4D

licence.name: subscription (stand-alone or inside the Maxon One bundle); Redshift included

engines.name: MoGraph
engines.does: Clone generators, effectors, fields and selection tags that duplicate and animate many objects at once.

engines.name: Fields
engines.does: Spatial strength distributions with layers and blend modes that drive effectors, deformers, volume builders, particle modifiers and vertex data.

engines.name: Scene Nodes
engines.does: A node graph that builds geometry, arrays, effectors and fields; the last output must reach the scene output.

engines.name: Volume Builder and Volume Mesher
engines.does: Turn objects into voxel volumes, combine them with Boolean operations and turn voxels back into a polygon surface.

engines.name: Simulation System
engines.does: Rigid body, cloth, soft body, balloon, rope and pyro tags that run in a shared simulation scene on CPU or GPU.

engines.name: Redshift
engines.does: GPU renderer that ships inside the product; lights, denoisers and a shader graph are part of it (renderer domain: realtime-render).

engines.name: Sketch and Toon
engines.does: Post effect and line materials for outline and cel-style output.

engines.name: BodyPaint 3D
engines.does: Texture painting and UV editing layouts built into the application.

engines.name: Python and C++ SDK
engines.does: Python API with generator, effector, field and tag plug-in types, plus a headless interpreter.

capabilities.does: Duplicates a child object in linear, radial, grid, honeycomb or object-surface layouts. Object mode places clones on points, edges, polygons, surface or volume. Clones can be instances, render instances or multi-instances.
capabilities.inputs: child object; optional target object or spline; effectors
capabilities.outputs: a set of clones with position, rotation and scale per clone

capabilities.does: Defines spatial strength values with field objects such as Spherical, Linear, Box, Random, Step, Shader, Sound and time-based fields. Layers combine with blend modes and remapping, and drive effectors, deformers, volume builders and vertex data.
capabilities.inputs: field objects or layers, remap settings
capabilities.outputs: strength values per point or clone

capabilities.does: Scene Nodes builds geometry from a graph of node categories such as Geometry, Array, Effectors, Fields, Flow Control, Operators and Distribution. Nodes can be grouped, and the last output must connect to the scene output.
capabilities.inputs: nodes from the asset list, bitmap images

capabilities.does: Voronoi Fracture breaks objects into fragments from points taken from polygons, splines, particles or textures. Options include Offset Fragments, Hull Only, Hollow Object, Scale Cells, N-gon surfaces and a Geometry Glue tab.
capabilities.inputs: closed mesh or spline, point sources, optional MoGraph weight map
capabilities.outputs: fragment geometry that effectors and dynamics can act on

capabilities.does: The Volume Builder converts objects into voxel volumes and combines them with Boolean operations. Several builders join into a Volume Set. Pressing C makes a Volume Object.
capabilities.inputs: closed polygon objects or splines as children

capabilities.does: The Volume Mesher turns voxels into a polygon surface through voxels that share one value, set by Surface Threshold. Resolution follows the Voxel Size of the Volume Builder.
capabilities.inputs: Volume Builder, Volume Set, Volume Object or Volume Loader as child

capabilities.does: The Remesh generator builds a second, cleaner mesh from a child object, usually uniform quads. Flow splines steer edge flow, and vertex maps, vertex colors and UVs carry over. Works best on organic shapes such as scans and sculpts.
The Subdivision Surfaces generator smooths a child polygon object into a finer surface; the generator list recommends it for smooth shapes such as characters.
The Boole generator combines child objects with Boolean operations; the generator list includes it next to Connect and Symmetry objects.
The Symmetry object, listed among the generators, mirrors a child object.
A child object placed under the Array object is copied around the array's origin in a spherical or a wave pattern. The Basic, Coord. and Object tabs hold its settings.
capabilities.inputs: child object; settings on the Basic, Coord. and Object tabs
capabilities.outputs: copies in a spherical or wave arrangement

capabilities.does: Extrude, Lathe, Loft and Sweep generators turn splines into surfaces. Lathe revolves a child spline through 360 degrees; Extrude suits 3D logos.
The Polygon Reduction generator lowers the polygon count of a child object; it sits in the same generator list as the LOD object.

Sculpting uses brushes on a subdivided mesh through a Sculpt tag. The Subdivide command raises polygon count to six figures. Sculpting layers are managed in the Sculpting Layer Manager, and brush presets include stamps and stencils.
Sculpt bake transfers displacement, normals and ambient occlusion from the sculpted object to a low-polygon mesh.
The UV Edit menu offers Relax UV, UV Peeler, Optimal Mapping, Remap, Realign, UV Terrace, Max UV and interactive mapping commands, among others.

BodyPaint 3D is built in with separate Paint and UVEdit layouts. With the classic renderer you paint in real time on the rendered image; with Redshift, painting tools work but real-time features are lost.
capabilities.inputs: object with UVs and material channels

capabilities.does: The Bake Material tag renders an object material to image files. It needs a UVW tag and outward normals, and does not support Node Materials. Outputs include colour, lighting, shadow, reflection, GI, ambient occlusion, normal and displacement maps.
capabilities.inputs: object with material tag and UVs

capabilities.does: Joint objects form a skeleton. Bones are the gaps between joints and a visual aid only. Joints carry the bone display and IK solving options.
capabilities.outputs: skeleton that drives a skin deformer

capabilities.does: The Weight tag stores per-point weights for linked joints or other objects, and the Skin object deforms the mesh from them. It works on polygon, spline, FFD and Bezier objects.

The Rigid Body tag simulates solid objects that follow gravity and collisions. Collision tags make non-simulated objects act as obstacles. Tags interact inside a Simulation Scene with settings for substeps, iterations and CPU or GPU device.

The Cloth tag simulates fabric on polygon objects with Thickness, Bendiness and Stretchiness settings. Cloth Belt connects cloth to unsimulated polygons, and Connector attaches cloth, rope and rigid bodies.
Soft Body and Balloon use the Cloth tag with different presets. A Mesh Deformer can transfer deformation from a low-resolution proxy to a high-resolution object.
The Rope tag, formerly Spline Dynamics, simulates splines with Bendiness and Stretchiness; Rope Belt anchors them to unsimulated polygon objects.
The Pyro and Pyro Fuel tags turn polygon or spline objects into emitters for smoke, fire and explosions; Pyro Fuel is preset for explosions.
The Timeline stores keys on tracks, one track per animated property, and interpolates between keys. Layers filter what is shown and objects can be locked.
Each track has an F-Curve that controls interpolation. The Timeline switches between Dope Sheet, F-Curve and Motion modes with Tab, and mini F-Curves sit under each track.

The Motion System stores animation as Motion Sources and applies instances as Motion Clips. Clips can be faded, looped, moved and scaled. Layers mix clips, and Bake Clips or Make Transition combine them.
The Redshift Light object offers Point, Spot, Infinite, Area, Dome, Photometric IES, Portal and Physical Sun types. Area shapes are Rectangle, Disc, Sphere, Cylinder and Mesh.
capabilities.inputs: light type, intensity, colour or temperature

capabilities.does: The Dome light surrounds the scene like a sky and can be mapped with an image.
The Project tab of the Redshift Light includes or excludes listed objects for light and shadow.
capabilities.inputs: object list, include or exclude mode

capabilities.does: Redshift offers three denoisers: Altus (single or dual pass, bucket mode only), NVIDIA OptiX (NVIDIA hardware) and Intel Open Image Denoise (all hardware). OptiX and OIDN work in progressive and bucket modes.
Redshift is the GPU-accelerated renderer included with each subscription, together with five Team Render nodes, according to the product page.

The legacy camera has focus distance, depth-of-field planes and DOF map blur, and a physical camera with focal length, shutter, F-stop, ISO and diaphragm. It also lists vignetting and chromatic aberration.
Camera tools include target camera, stereo camera, Align To Spline tag, Motion Camera tag, Morph Camera tag and Stage object.
Redshift materials are built in a Shader Graph. MoGraph clone data can be read with Color, Scalar and Integer User Data nodes; Shader Switch and RS Mod pick or wrap values.

Sketch and Toon draws lines with Sketch materials that have tabs for strokes, colour, thickness, opacity and distort. Materials are assigned globally, per object through a Sketch Style tag, or by an assignment box.

The Python API manuals cover the console, script manager, plug-in types such as ObjectData and NodeData, the MAXON API and the Asset API, with scripting objects for generators, effectors, fields, tags and Xpresso nodes.
A Python Generator object builds geometry in its main function and returns one object, or a null that holds several. The documentation advises cloning rather than modifying scene objects.
c4dpy is a headless Cinema 4D instance and Python interpreter that loads and saves files, builds scenes, starts renders and runs plug-ins without the GUI.

The FBX exporter has options for file version, text or binary, selection only, lights, cameras, splines, instances, Catmull-Clark subdivision, normals, vertex colours, track baking, material baking, embedded textures, up axis and LOD suffix.

The glTF exporter writes glTF text or GLB binary with PSR, morph and skin animation (maximum four joint weights per point), baked dynamics, cameras, normals and the first UV map. Shaders must be baked.
USD import offers presets and settings, geometry and animation groups; USD export adds a materials group.

Cineware loads .c4d files as layers in After Effects, renders them with the Cinema 4D engine and offers Software, Standard Draft, Standard Final and OpenGL modes. Multi-pass output creates layers per render element.

Team Render shares work among networked computers running the same Cinema 4D version. Clients take whole frames of an animation, or buckets of one still. Stereoscopic and sound rendering are not supported.

scripting: Python Generator, Effector and Field plug-in objects
outcomes: baked meshes and textures for games

rea.notes: Closed core; public user manual plus Python and C++ SDK documentation. The vendor page named 2027.0 as the release in preparation on 2026-11-02; manual pages cited come from S22 to 2026 releases, so menu names may differ between versions. The USD page body was behind a very large navigation block, so only the option group names were read.

entries.name: Houdini

licence.name: editions FX, Core, Indie and Education; Apprentice free trial; Houdini Engine sold separately

engines.name: SOPs (geometry nodes)
engines.does: Node network for procedural geometry: modelling, attributes, groups, UVs, volumes, hair, terrain and rigging nodes.

engines.name: DOPs (dynamics)
engines.does: Solver network for rigid bodies, particles, FLIP and gas fluids, pyro, cloth, finite elements, wires, crowds and ripples.

engines.name: VEX and VOPs
engines.does: Compiled expression language and its node form, used in wrangles, shading, volumes, particles and channels.

engines.name: Solaris (LOPs)
engines.does: Scene assembly, look development and lighting on USD, with Karma as the renderer.

engines.name: Karma
engines.does: Houdini renderer with CPU and XPU render delegates, used from Solaris (renderer domain: realtime-render).

engines.name: PDG and TOPs
engines.does: Task graph with work items, dependencies, schedulers and partitioners for distributed jobs.

engines.name: Vellum
engines.does: Position-based solver for cloth, hair, grains, fluids and soft bodies.

engines.name: KineFX and APEX
engines.does: Geometry-level rigging and animation framework with a graph evaluation system for rigs.

engines.name: CHOPs
engines.does: Channel network for animation curves and audio data.

engines.name: Copernicus (COPs)
engines.does: GPU image processing framework for 2D and 3D image work inside Houdini.

engines.name: Houdini Engine
engines.does: API layer (Python wrapper, C API, SessionSync) that runs Houdini assets in other hosts.

capabilities.does: SOP networks build geometry from nodes for attributes, groups, curves, volumes, conversion, deformation, hair, terrain and rigging. The node index lists several hundred nodes in these families.
Poly Extrude extrudes polygonal faces and edges; Extrude Volume is a separate node for volumes.
capabilities.inputs: polygon geometry, face or edge group

capabilities.does: The Boolean SOP combines meshes; Boolean Fracture is a separate SOP in the same index.

PolyBevel adds fillet polygons along selected edges, around selected points and at polyline corners. Distance sets the size, Divisions the number of rows, and Shape chooses none, solid, crease, chamfer or round; a Profile ramp or curve shapes round fillets.
Mirror duplicates and mirrors geometry across a mirror plane.
Lattice Deform deforms geometry by how the user reshapes control geometry.
Subdivide turns polygons into smoother, higher-resolution polygons.
PolyReduce lowers the polygon count of a model while keeping its shape.
Quad Remesh converts an arbitrary mesh into structured quadrilaterals; Remesh instead rebuilds the surface with near-equilateral triangles.
Sculpt 2.0 applies brush strokes to a surface interactively, with operations such as Clay, Inflate, Flatten, Smooth, Relax, Crease and Pinch. Edits are stored in an internal Sculpt Stash.
Scatter places random points on a surface or through a volume; Copy to Points, Copy to Curves and Instance place geometry on them.
capabilities.inputs: surface or volume, geometry to copy

capabilities.does: VDB nodes convert polygons to VDB volumes (VDB from Polygons), smooth them (VDB Smooth) and combine two volumes (VDB Combine). Volume Wrangle and Volume VOP edit voxel values with VEX.
UV Flatten makes flattened pieces in texture space, UV Unwrap separates UVs into flat non-overlapping groups, and UV Project assigns UVs by projection from a set direction.

UV Layout fits UV islands into targets: the unit square, custom rectangles, UDIM tiles or the islands of a second input. Controls include scale mode, island padding, rotation step, axis alignment and stacking of identical islands.
Heightfield nodes cover noise, masks, erosion (hydro, thermal, precipitation), flow, slump, terracing, scatter and project. Terrain is a 2D grid of layers with a base height layer and mask layers.
The SOP list includes an L-System node and Labs biome nodes (plant define, plant scatter, region assign) for procedural plants and vegetation placement.
Labs nodes include a Building Generator and utility node for procedural buildings.
Cloud nodes generate cloud shapes from lines, polygons or intersections, add billowy or wispy noise, adjust density profiles and light clouds.
Labs AV nodes cover image analysis, structure from motion, depth maps, meshing and texturing for photogrammetry.
VEX is a compiled expression language, loosely based on C, used for shading, point attribute edits, particles, channels and compositing. VOP networks compile to VEX.
The hou module gives scripts access to nodes, parameters, geometry, dynamics, crowds, digital assets, shelf tools, viewports and utility types such as Vector3 and Matrix4.
TOPs and PDG split large jobs into work items with dependencies. Processors fan out items, partitioners group them, and schedulers (local or HQueue farm) run them.
Solaris uses LOP nodes to generate and modify USD for characters, props, lighting and rendering, with component building, materials, variants and payloads.
The Solaris section covers writing USD to disk, as well as USD basics for scenes.
The Karma user guide covers geometry, lights, cameras, motion blur, materials, texture maps, sampling and noise, with CPU and XPU render delegates.
Solaris look development covers MaterialX, UDIM paths, shader translation and shot-building tools.
Vellum simulates cloth with stitch and sliding constraints, plasticity, tearing and draping; DOPs also have a Cloth Object and Cloth Solver.
Vellum softbodies use tetrahedral stretch and shape-matching constraints; DOPs add finite-element solid and soft body solvers.
Vellum is named as a solver for hair as well as cloth, grains, fluids and soft bodies; DOPs include a Wire Solver and POP Hair Internal Force.
Vellum muscle nodes set muscle constraints and properties and compute the muscle and skin passes.
The Grains toolset simulates sand and other granular matter with Position Based Dynamics.
FLIP nodes (source, boundary, collide, container, solver) simulate liquids; DOPs also list particle fluids, SDF fluid solver and Whitewater.
Pyro covers smoke, fire and explosions with a sparse solver, sourcing, flames, instancing and Pyro Configure presets for fire, fireball, candle, smoke plumes and dry ice.
The oceans section covers ocean spectra, Whitewater (SOP and DOP), a Shallow Water Solver for flooding heightfields, and a Ripple solver.
POP nodes add sources, forces, collisions, steering, flocking, grains, fluid, sprites, instances and speed limits to particle systems.
DOP force nodes include Gravity, Wind, Vortex, Drag, Fan, Magnet, Point, Uniform and Field Force.
DOPs provide RBD objects, packed objects, solver, constraints (pin, hinge, spring, angular), keyframe-active and auto freeze for rigid body simulation.

The destruction toolset covers RBD material fracturing for concrete, glass and wood, custom cutters, constraints, guided simulations and car destruction. The Voronoi Fracture SOP fractures from cell points.
Crowd tools cover agents, states, triggers, transition graphs, layered animation clips, terrain adaptation and foot planting, ragdolls and caches.
Guide and fur nodes include Guide Groom, Hair Generate, Hair Card Generate, Draw Guides, Hair Clump and Groom Blend; Feather nodes build and deform feathers.
KineFX skeleton tools create a skeleton, orient its joints, mirror and blend skeletons, and add tags and properties that prepare it for rigging.
The APEX AutoRig Builder and AutoRig Component nodes apply prebuilt rig components to characters.
Capture weights for skin deformation are made with Joint Capture Paint, Biharmonic and Proximity nodes; Joint Deform applies them.
KineFX offers IK Chains and Full Body IK nodes, with FBIK Configure Targets for the animate state.
Character Blend Shapes nodes and the Blend Shapes SOP handle shape-based deformation.
KineFX retargeting transfers animation between skeletons or rigs; Biped Retarget and Extract Locomotion are named SOPs.
KineFX imports motion capture data and edits it as MotionClips; FBX and glTF animation import nodes bring clips in.
APEX Add ML Deformer and Agent Add ML Deformer nodes attach machine-learning deformers to characters and agents.
CHOPs process time-based channel data such as animation curves and audio with nodes like Blend, Lag, Spring, Noise, Wave, Filter and Math; export flags route channels to parameters.
Copernicus is a GPU framework for 2D and 3D image processing, with topics for dynamics, machine learning and advanced concepts.
Alembic files are a listed import and export topic; SOPs include Alembic, Alembic Group and Alembic Primitive nodes.
FBX (Filmbox) files are a listed import and export topic; a Filmbox FBX ROP node writes them and KineFX has FBX character, skin and animation import nodes.
The I/O topics list an Import and export glTF page for moving glTF files into and out of Houdini.
Houdini Engine has a Python API (wrapper of the HAPI API), a C API and a SessionSync utility that runs a Houdini Engine session inside Houdini.

scripting: Houdini Engine C and Python APIs
outcomes: simulation caches (fluids, pyro, destruction, cloth, crowds)
Houdini digital assets for game engines
