Some SOP node names came from a node index that was read in three 100000-character slices; the DOP list names are as printed on the index.

entries.name: ZBrush

licence.name: subscription; also inside the Maxon One bundle

engines.name: Sculptris Pro
engines.does: Mode that adds and removes triangles under the brush while sculpting.

engines.name: DynaMesh
engines.does: Remeshing that rebuilds a sculpt as evenly spaced polygons at a set resolution.

engines.name: ZRemesher
engines.does: One-click retopology with a global polygon count and guide curves.

engines.name: ZModeler
engines.does: Polygon modelling brush with polygon, edge and point actions.

engines.name: Live Boolean
engines.does: Real-time preview of add, subtract and intersect operations between SubTools.

engines.name: Redshift in ZBrush
engines.does: CPU Redshift rendering with BPR (Best Preview Render), included with the subscription (renderer domain: realtime-render).

capabilities.does: Sculptris Pro changes the model topology under the brush as it sculpts: dense triangles for a small draw size, sparse for a large one, with real-time decimation when smoothing. It needs a model without subdivision levels.
capabilities.inputs: polymesh without subdivision levels, brush strokes
capabilities.outputs: same model with polygons added or removed

capabilities.does: DynaMesh regenerates evenly distributed polygons from a sculpt. Resolution sets density, Group keeps PolyGroup shells, and inserted meshes merge (Add), subtract (Sub) or intersect (And) on remesh. A Ctrl-drag on empty canvas updates it.

ZRemesher recreates a model with controlled polygon flow and a global polycount in one click. Curves drawn on the model steer edge loops, PolyPaint can control density, and Freeze Border keeps openings.
The Geometry palette holds subdivision levels with Divide, SDiv, Lower Res, Higher Res, Del Lower and Del Higher, plus Smt for smoothing during division.
Dynamic Subdiv shows a subdivided preview of the mesh without changing it, with Flat Subdivision, Smooth Subdivision and Apply options; MicroPoly and ClayPolish sit in the same palette.
capabilities.outputs: dynamic subdivision preview or applied mesh

capabilities.does: Ships with over 30 startup 3D brushes and accepts custom brushes. Vector Displacement Mesh brushes stamp sculpts with overhangs, Alpha 3D turns a sculpt into a 2D alpha, and Lazy Mouse 2.0 smooths stroke angle and length.
3D Layers keep several detail stages in one model, each toggled or adjusted independently.

Surface Noise adds noise to a whole model or to selected areas whatever the polycount; the NoiseMaker plug-in offers parametric generators such as camouflage, scales and hex tiles, and images can be loaded as alphas in its preview.
HD Geometry subdivides models up to about a billion polygons while concentrating detail where it is sculpted.
Deformations such as twist, stretch and bend apply to any mesh along any axis.
Transpose isolates part of a model with a mask and poses, scales or rotates it without a rig.
ZModeler Extrude pulls targeted polygons by click and drag; QMesh extrudes polygons that try to fuse with neighbours.
ZModeler Bevel slices edges into angled planes; size is set by dragging. Crease marks edges for creasing.
ZModeler Inset inserts smaller polygons inside targeted polygons, connected to the originals.
Insert Polyloops adds one or more edge loops that follow the topology of the target region.
The ZModeler Mask action masks clicked polygons to protect them from changes; PolyGroup, Equalize, Spherize, Inflate, Bridge and Spin are other actions in the list.

Live Boolean previews addition, subtraction and intersection between SubTools in real time while objects are moved or sculpted. Make Boolean Mesh builds a new tool. Primitives, ZSpheres and ZSketches must be converted first.
capabilities.inputs: SubTools set to add, subtract or intersect

capabilities.does: Decimation Master lowers polygon count in three steps: options, pre-process and decimate. It can keep UVs, set quality from 100 percent down to 0.01 percent or a target count, and exports all SubTools as one OBJ.
capabilities.inputs: sculpted model, quality or target count

capabilities.does: SubTools split a model into independent parts. Split Hidden, Split Masked and Split Unmasked separate geometry; MergeDown and MergeVisible combine SubTools; folders group them.
SubTool Extract builds a new mesh from a masked or hidden area, with S Smt, Thick, Double, TCorner and TBorder options, previewed until accepted.
ZSpheres build a base mesh by moving, rotating and scaling spheres, then skin it for sculpting. ZSketch lets spheres be drawn freely in 3D space, and Mannequins are posable ZSphere armatures.
ShadowBox generates a mesh from silhouettes painted on the sides of a box.
Spotlight edits imported images and projects them onto the model with sculpting and painting brushes; v2.0 with Snapshot3D converts grayscale alphas into 3D models for addition or subtraction.

Polypaint stores colour on vertices, so quality follows active point count. Fill Object, primary and secondary colours, Spray strokes and alphas paint the model; raise DynaMesh resolution for more detail.
UV Master is a plug-in that generates UVs for a model in one click, ready for painting in a 2D program.

Vector displacement maps store RGB direction per pixel, so surfaces move in any direction. Options include tangent or world space, 16-bit or 32-bit, and smoothing of UVs and normals; output is TIFF or OpenEXR.
capabilities.inputs: model with subdivision levels and UVs

capabilities.does: FiberMesh grows fibres, hair, fur or vegetation as real geometry from masked areas, added as a new SubTool. Groom brushes shape it and slicing or subdividing converts it to a regular polymesh.
ArrayMesh duplicates the model into instances controlled by Offset, Scale, Rotate and Pivot (each with a curve), Repeat count and TransPose; Make Mesh converts the array into editable geometry.
NanoMesh creates many instances of an object while keeping polygon count low.
Cloth simulation with collision detection, and cloth brushes that shape the result directly.
Curve brushes such as Curve Flat, Curve Tube, Snake Curve and CurveAlpha, plus MeshFromMask for lasso, circle, rectangle and curve shapes, were added in release 2021.6.

Python scripts import zbrush.commands and send commands to ZBrush native command sequences. They cannot read ZBrush data directly. A Zscript Python sub-palette loads scripts and macros, and batch mode runs a script from the command line.
Imports and exports Wavefront OBJ, and exports Maya ASCII and Web3D X3D files; Mesh Ascii and binary files import.
FBX import and export runs through the FBX Export Import plug-in.
STL and VRML export runs through the 3D Print Hub plug-in.
Universal Scene Description support was added in release 2021.6 and is listed among the import and export formats.
GoZ moves a model to a supported application and back; the product page also names GoZ for work moving to Cinema 4D and Cineware for After Effects.
Redshift in ZBrush renders on the CPU together with BPR (Best Preview Render); Redshift CPU is included in every subscription according to the product page.

outcomes: displacement, vector displacement and normal maps

rea.notes: Closed core. User guide pages used here are from several ZBrush versions (2021 to current help site); the vendor page named 2027.0 as the latest release on 2026-11-02. ZBrush 2021.6 release notes cited for Curve brushes and USD.

entries.name: 3D-Coat (3DCoat)

licence.name: paid licence (node-locked or floating) with 30-day trial; free 3DCoatPrint and Textura learning versions

engines.name: Voxel sculpting
engines.does: Sculpting on voxels without topology limits, plus Boolean operations.

engines.name: Retopo and AUTOPO
engines.does: Manual retopology tools and automatic retopology driven by edge loops the user defines.

capabilities.does: Voxel sculpting with no topological constraints; the feature list also names Boolean operations and a concept-art workflow based on voxels.
Dozens of sculpting brushes with adaptive dynamic tessellation.
Boolean operations between shapes that keep crisp edges.
Classic polygon modelling with Move, Rotate, Scale, Extrude and Inset tools; splines and joints give a fast curve-based modelling method.
Manual retopology tools with retopo groups, and AUTOPO automatic retopology driven by user-defined edge loops.
An advanced baking settings dialog is listed under the Retopo tools.
UV-set creation and editing with multiple UV sets, Global Uniform unwrapping, and ABF, LSCM and Planar algorithms.
Painting by Microvertex, per-pixel or Ptex approaches, with texture sizes up to 16K.
A real-time PBR viewport with HDR lighting; Smart Materials have easy setup options.
A free PBR library of 500+ scanned materials and 1,200+ samples up to 8K, with 120 free points per month.
The features page says users can write scripts for quick repeated actions and can record scripts while working with primitives. It does not mention batch processing of files.
Release 2026.11 announces GPU node-based texturing with editable materials, masks, filters and procedural effects, and about 30 material channels.
Release 2026.11 announces LWO3 import and GLB export.

rea.notes: Closed core. Capabilities come from the vendor feature page and the home page release notice (2026.11), not a manual; basis is observed. The feature page still mentions version 4 serials, so some wording is old.

licence.name: paid plug-in for Cinema 4D (Insydium Fused subscriptions exist; terms not read)

engines.name: xpFluidFLIP
engines.does: APIC and FLIP fluid solvers with a collision system for fast or rotating colliders.

capabilities.does: ParticleFX combines emitters and modifiers for motion graphics effects inside Cinema 4D.
Smoke, fire and explosion simulation with advection; ExplosiaFX can be exported as a VDB volume.
xpFluidFLIP uses APIC and FLIP solvers with a collision system for fast-moving or rotating colliders.
Grain solvers cover granular materials and splash effects such as ocean spray.
DynamicsFX provides dynamic motion and destruction effects.
ClothFX drives cloth with any modifier and offers advanced tearing options.
xpScatter scatters objects across splines and parametric objects, with topology controls for slope, height and curvature.
Supports OpenVDB export, particle caching (xpCache) with time and spline retiming, and data import and export.

entries.name: Gaea

licence.name: free download plus paid editions (page shows a one-time price of 199 USD; editions not read)

engines.name: Simulate nodes
engines.does: Erosion, thermal breakdown, debris, sediment, water, snow, glacier and vegetation simulation nodes.

capabilities.does: The node reference groups nodes into ten families: Primitive, Terrain, Modify, Surface, Simulate, Derive, Colorize, Output, Utility and Macro.
Erosion nodes include Erosion, Erosion2, EasyErosion and Wizard; Thermal, Debris, Scree and Sediments handle breakdown and deposition.
capabilities.outputs: eroded terrain, flow and deposition maps

capabilities.does: Lake, Rivers, Sea and HydroFix nodes add water behaviour to terrain.
Snow, Snowfield, Glacier and IceFloe nodes add cold-climate effects.
Trees and Shrubs nodes simulate vegetation on terrain.
Derive nodes analyse a terrain's surface structure, slope, height, flow, curvature, normals or colour and turn the result into masks and supporting data maps.
The TextureBaker output node bakes derived texture maps from terrain data.
Output nodes include Export, Mesher, Unity and Unreal for engine-ready output.
The node reference has a Macro family that shows the user's installed custom macros as nodes that can be reused in a graph.

entries.name: Substance 3D Painter

licence.name: subscription (Substance 3D Collection, 30-day trial); no standalone price listed on the product page

engines.name: Painting engine
engines.does: Applies brush strokes, particles and projections to texture sets in a non-destructive layer stack; strokes are kept in 3D so they can be recomputed.

engines.name: Mesh map bakers
engines.does: Computes maps such as thickness, bent normals and ID maps from a high-poly mesh or the low-poly mesh itself.

engines.name: Iray renderer mode
engines.does: A render mode switched on with F10 that shares display settings with the normal viewport.

engines.name: Real-time viewport with sparse virtual textures
engines.does: Streams only the texture parts needed for the current view to hold GPU memory down on projects with many texture sets.

engines.name: Shader API
engines.does: Library set and example shaders (PBR metal rough, PBR material layering, toon, pixelated, surface shader) that define how channels are shown in the viewport.

capabilities.does: The paint tool puts a chosen material on the mesh with brush strokes, and the eraser takes painted data away again.
capabilities.outputs: paint data on the layer channels

capabilities.does: The Projection tool stamps a material or texture through the current camera view onto the mesh.
Polygon Fill builds masks from picked mesh polygons, so a mask follows the geometry.
Smudge drags existing paint along the stroke, smearing colour and other material values together.
Clone samples material from one place on the mesh and paints it onto another, to copy or patch an area.
Quick Mask gives a short-lived mask that restricts where paint goes. A Material Picker tool listed beside it samples material properties from the mesh surface.
The Path tool lays a curve over the mesh and applies strokes along it: painting, erasing, blurring, or adding fine details like zippers and cracks.
Straight Line lets any painting tool draw a ruler-straight stroke from two clicks.
Lazy Mouse lags the paint point behind the cursor by a set distance, which smooths shaky strokes.

Symmetry repeats brush strokes, or a whole fill layer, around an axis. The contextual toolbar switches it on and holds its settings; mirror and radial are the two types. It is not available for paint or stencil projection in the 2D view.

A fill layer or fill effect places a texture on the mesh with a chosen projection mode, so little hand painting is needed. Modes: per-UV-tile fill, UV, tri-planar, planar, spherical, cylindrical and warp; settings are in Properties.
capabilities.outputs: tiled or projected texture on the layer

capabilities.does: A dynamic stroke is a brush driven by a Substance file; each stamp along the stroke can vary according to the logic authored in that file.
Particles are a brush type; the guide covers presets and a particle editor with scripts for creating new particle behaviours.

Only bitmap-based presets in Photoshop ABR files import into Painter; procedural, airbrush, bristle, erodible, pencil, mixer, clone stamp and smudge presets are skipped. Shape dynamics, scattering and transfer settings map to Paint tool controls; texture, dual brush and color dynamics do not.

Some default shader channels can be painted directly for effects such as height detail that is converted to a normal map; the guide lists ambient occlusion, flow map, height map and normal map painting.
capabilities.outputs: painted AO, flow, height or normal data

capabilities.does: The layer stack holds paint layers (brush and particle painting), fill layers (a material fills the channels) and folders. Each layer is multi-channel with its own blending mode and opacity per channel.
Any layer can get a mask: white, black, bitmap, colour selection or height combination. Masks are painted in grayscale or driven by filters and Substance graphs.

Effects are added to a layer or mask through the right-click menu or the button above the layer stack. The page lists seven types: Generator, Paint, Fill, Levels, Compare Mask, Filter and Anchor Point.
Smart materials and smart masks are saved layer-stack presets. They carry a texturing process from one texture set or project to another and adapt the result to the mesh topology.
capabilities.outputs: layered material adapted to the mesh

capabilities.does: Generic materials are blended inside a shader instead of baked into one texture. The default pbr-material-layering shader blends 4 materials with 3 masks, and shader parameters can be exported as JSON.
capabilities.outputs: tiled material blend, JSON of the setup

capabilities.does: Baking mode (F8) bakes mesh maps from high-poly meshes or the low-poly mesh itself. Cage options: distance based, automatic (experimental) or a custom file. A baking log lists errors.
capabilities.inputs: low-poly mesh, optional high-poly files, bakers
capabilities.outputs: baked mesh maps per texture set or UV tile

capabilities.does: The ID map baker takes colour from vertex colour, material colour, file ID or mesh ID/polygroup; for the last two, colours are generated randomly, by hue shift or in grayscale.
capabilities.inputs: high-poly or low-poly mesh with IDs

capabilities.does: The thickness baker casts secondary rays between a minimum and maximum occluder distance with a spread angle and distribution, and can use distances relative to the bounding box.
Automatic UV unwrapping makes UV islands on import for meshes without UVs. Seam setting: generate missing data only, or recompute all.
capabilities.outputs: mesh with generated seams and UV islands

capabilities.does: UV Tiles give each UV range its own texture set, which raises effective resolution. They follow the UDIM naming convention; resolution can be set per tile, and image sequences can be imported.
When texture resolution changes or a new mesh is loaded, painting is reprojected from world-space data onto the new mesh. A preserve-stroke option controls how the bounding box is normalised.
Materials can carry a real-world size; with physical size enabled on a fill layer the texture matches real scale. Internal unit is centimetres, and mesh units are converted on import.
capabilities.inputs: material with physical size, mesh units

capabilities.does: Export Textures (Ctrl+Shift+E) writes bitmaps through output templates that control file naming, channel packing, file format and bit depth; dozens of defaults target common 3D applications.
Export Mesh writes the changed mesh, with or without displacement tessellation. Options: apply triangulation, and recompute vertex normals after tessellation.
USD support covers creating a project with scope and variant choice, subdivision levels and animation frames, exporting materials and textures as USD, and USD as a mesh-only export format.
capabilities.outputs: USD materials and textures, USD mesh

capabilities.does: The viewport streams in only the texture parts visible from the current view (since version 2018.3), keeping GPU memory use steady on projects with many texture sets or UDIMs.
A separate Iray mode renders the project with the Iray engine. It is toggled with F10 (F9 returns to painting), the camera icon or the Mode menu; display settings match the normal viewport.
Subsurface scattering works in the real-time viewport and in the Iray renderer, with a dedicated material type and parameters.
Viewport post effects: colour correction, depth of field, glare, lens distortion, tone mapping, vignette and colour profile.
Colour management uses OpenColorIO version 2 and is enabled per project. The page lists which channels are colour managed, such as base colour, diffuse and coat colour, and which are not.
JavaScript plugins use QML and the Painter API; the guide's example adds a toolbar button that exports textures with padding, dithering, resolution and bit-depth settings.
capabilities.inputs: plugin script in the plugins folder

capabilities.does: The product page names Python scripting among Painter's pipeline features, beside multi-tile (UDIM) painting, Alembic import and camera import, and says Painter follows the VFX Reference Platform.
Shader API reference with function libraries (PBR, anisotropic PBR, POM, SSS, sparse textures and more) and shaders such as PBR metal rough, PBR material layering, toon and pixelated.

SVG and Illustrator (.ai) files import like ordinary images and are converted to pixels non-destructively. Resolution can follow the texture set (Auto), the file's own size (Asset) or a custom value; artboard, crop area and scope settings limit what renders.

outcomes: PBR texture sets for game engines and renderers
UDIM texture sets for film assets
layered-material mask maps with JSON setup

entries.name: Substance 3D Designer

licence.name: subscription (Substance 3D Collection, free trial)

engines.name: Substance graph engine
engines.does: Evaluates node graphs that generate and process 2D image data not tied to a fixed resolution, colour or shape.

engines.name: Function graphs
engines.does: Node graphs that process single values (integers, floats, vectors) with maths nodes; used for exposed-parameter behaviour, Pixel Processors and FX-Maps.

engines.name: MDL graph editor
engines.does: Authors MDL materials and previews them in real time; the result is a portable material definition.

engines.name: 3D view
engines.does: Shows materials on standard and extended primitives or custom meshes, with selectable 3D renderers and camera post effects.

capabilities.does: Substance graphs are node networks that generate and process 2D image data without a fixed resolution, colour or shape, so one graph can serve many outputs.
Function graphs work on single values, not pixels, with maths nodes and no thumbnails. They drive exposed parameters, Pixel Processors and FX-Maps and supply values inside graphs.

An FX-Map builds a procedural image by repeatedly copying, subdividing, moving and blending it. Quadrant nodes add quad-tree levels, Iterate nodes repeat the input, and function graphs steer the motion with variables such as $number.

The Noises category holds 3D and 2D generators such as Perlin, Simplex, Worley, Voronoi, Plasma, Cells, Clouds, white noise, moisture noise, liquid and caustics, plus numbered Grunge Map nodes and named grunge variants for scratches, rust, spots and splashes.
The Patterns category includes Brick Generator, Tile Generator, Weave Generator, Scratches Generator, Shape, Stripes, Checker 1, Star, Polygon, several gradients and a Triangle Grid.

Patterns also holds Tile Sampler, Splatter, Splatter Circular and Shape Splatter, with Blend, Data Extract and To Mask variants of Shape Splatter; by name they scatter shapes or inputs over an area. Parameters were not read.
capabilities.inputs: shape or image inputs, scatter parameters

capabilities.does: Normal map nodes include bent normal, normal blend, combine, invert, normalize, sobel, uncombine, vector rotation, normal-to-height (also HQ), normal transform and height-to-normal in world units.
Tiling filters make a photo or a patch repeat without a visible seam: Make It Tile Patch and Make It Tile Photo. The scan-processing group adds Smart Auto Tile.

The Scan Processing group of material filters lists AO Cancellation, Atlas Scatter, Atlas Splitter, Clone Patch, Color Equalizer, Crop, Material Clone Patch, Multi-Angle to Albedo and to Normal, Multi Clone Patch, Multi Crop and Smart Auto Tile.

Mesh-based mask generators are a node group that includes Cloth Wear, Dirt, Dripping Rust, Dust, Edge Damages, Edge Dirt, Edge Wear, Grease, Leaks, Leather Wear, Metal Edge Wear, Paint Wear, Sun Bleach and more.
capabilities.inputs: mesh data (implied by the category name)

capabilities.does: Weathering generators cover cracks, fabric, leather, metal, moss, rock and rust. A utilities group adds Material Selector, Material Mesh Data Blender, Mesh Data Combiner, Tri Planar and 3D Planar Projection.

The guide has a Bakers section and a legacy bakers interface page; the mesh-based generator category (mesh data combiner, material mesh data blender) suggests baked mesh data as input. Pages not read.

The spline node group creates splines (Cubic, Poly Quadratic, Circle, Fill, Paths to Spline), edits them (2D Transform, Append, Select, Warp), bridges and merges them, scatters and maps content along them, and renders them or samples height and thickness.
capabilities.outputs: rendered or mapped spline images, warped paths

capabilities.does: The HDRI Tools group builds and fixes environment lights: Blackbody, Color Temperature Adjustment, Exposure, HDR Merge, Nadir Extract and Nadir Patch, Panorama Rotation, Physical Sun/Sky, Line, Plane, Shape and Sphere lights, Straighten Horizon.

Substance Archives (SBSAR) are compiled, optimised Substance files: faster to compute, graph locked, parameters still tweakable. They run in Painter and other apps with a Substance integration, such as Maya, 3ds Max, Unreal and Unity.
Authors build their own control panel for a graph by exposing parameters; the guide covers parameter presets, visible-if expressions and inheritance between graphs.
A graph can be exported as bitmaps or as PSD files; Substance files stay the editable source and bitmaps serve targets without Substance support.
Graphs can be reused as instances and subgraphs, so a built-up material or filter becomes a node inside another graph with its own exposed controls.

The 3D view shows materials on standard primitives (cube, cylinder, plane, sphere, hollow box) and extended ones (cloth, mat ball, rounded cube, torus), with wireframe, bounding box, tangent-space gizmos and UV overlay.
Graphs can work with 3D scene resources: override scene materials, extract material values and textures, and export scenes; other resources include bitmaps, SVG, AxF and fonts.
capabilities.outputs: scene with replaced materials, extracted textures

capabilities.does: The product page names Pantone and OpenColorIO colour management support.

Atomic nodes are the base nodes that all other library nodes are built from. The page lists Blend, Blur, Channels Shuffle, Curve, Directional Blur, Directional Warp, Distance, Emboss, FX-Map, Gradient Map, Grayscale Conversion, HSL, Levels, Pixel Processor, Sharpen, Warp and others.

The Effects filters include ambient occlusion (HBAO and RTAO), Bevel, Curvature with Smooth and Sobel variants, Diffusion, Edge Detect, Emboss With Gloss, Swirl, Uber Emboss, Vector Warp and Vector Morph.
Project configuration files (SBSPRJ, SBSCFG), user preference setup and environment variables let a studio automate Designer setup.
The product page mentions an extensive set of APIs for building and sharing plugins and utility graphs. Python API pages were not opened.

scripting: APIs for plugins and utility graphs (see product page)

entries.name: Substance 3D Sampler

licence.name: subscription (Substance 3D Collection)

engines.name: Image to Material
engines.does: Turns a single photo into PBR channels with an AI algorithm or a procedural Bitmap-to-Material algorithm.

engines.name: Filters and generators from Designer
engines.does: Material layers use filters and generators shared with Designer.

capabilities.does: Image to Material builds a PBR material from one image. The AI algorithm finds shapes to make normal, height and roughness maps and removes shadows from albedo; the B2M algorithm is procedural and less exact.

The Delight (AI Powered) tool removes lighting information from the base color channel and has no parameters. It goes at the top of the layer stack and suits the Image to Material route; Image to Material (AI powered) already includes its own delighting step.
Layer parameters can be exposed from the Properties panel and exported with the material. Image to Material, Content-Aware Fill, Normal to Height and Upscale parameters cannot be exposed.
The Export panel writes the material as SBSAR or SBS with its exposed parameters, for use in any software that reads SBSAR.
Physical size can be set from a manual measure between two points or an auto measure based on image dpi; exports keep the size in SBSAR metadata or in image ratio.

Generator filters add pattern content to a material. The docs split them into converting ones (Brickwall, Floor Tiles, Panel, Parquet, Pavement, Quilt Stitch, Stonewall, Surface Relief) and adding ones (Atlas Scatter, Decal, Embossing, Embroidery, Gravel, Pattern, Perforate, Splatter, Weave, Cloth Weave).
Wear and Finish filters age or dress a material. Listed filters: Corrode, Cracks, Dirt, Discarded Gums, Dust, Erode, Metal Finish, Moss, Oxidate, Paint, Rust, Scratch, Snow, Water and Varnish.
The physical-size workflow page uses Equalize to remove gradients, Tiling to fix seams and Warp Transform to realign parts of a scan; a Make it Tile tool is also listed.

HDRI Tools are filters for environment lights: Color Temperature Adjustment, Exposure, Exposure Preview, HDR Merge, Nadir Extract and Patch, Panorama Patch, Straighten Horizon, and Line, Plane, Shape and Sphere lights. A notice says environment lights and these tools end with Sampler 5.2.
The product FAQ says 3D capture makes textured 3D meshes from photos.

Default export presets pack and name textures for Arnold 5, Blender Cycles/Eevee, Corona Renderer, Enscape (Revit), KeyShot 9+, Lens Studio, Spark AR Studio, Unity HDRP and Unity (standard and specular), Unreal Engine 4, Redshift and V-Ray Next.

Sampler supports custom plugins through its Python API, with guides for plugins (Python and QML) and for scripts (Python). The full API documentation is installed with the program, and a page covers managing installed plugins and scripts.
Edit in Photoshop sends an image to Photoshop and brings the edits back into Sampler.

Tools are Sampler's largest filter group, mostly for fixing technical issues in materials. The page lists Channels Generation, Channel Switch, Height to AO, Height to Normal, Normal to Height, PBR Validate, Perspective Correction, Clone Stamp, Crop, Upscale, Atlas Creator and Atlas Splitter, without descriptions.

Customisable materials change the surface properties of objects in the scene.
The guide lists material displacement, material projections and applying images to models as separate features.

capabilities.inputs: not stated in the pages read
capabilities.outputs: not stated in the pages read

entries.name: Substance 3D Modeler

licence.name: subscription (Substance 3D Collection); a free public beta page exists

engines.name: Signed distance field clay
engines.does: Stores 3D space as a grid of voxels holding distance to the nearest surface and an inside/outside flag, instead of polygons.

capabilities.does: Clay is the default tool and the only one that creates clay from nothing; Erase removes it, Buildup and Inflate add to surfaces, and the tool list also has Crease and Flatten.
Warp pulls and bends existing clay; in VR it follows full six-degree hand motion, so one stroke can move, turn and scale. Elastic and Smooth tools sit alongside it.
Split moves clay into separate layers. Crop keeps only the clay the brush touches and removes the rest, the opposite of Erase.
The Paint tool adds colour to clay, which can be exported as vertex colours depending on export settings.
Symmetry inside a layer duplicates strokes: mirror across a plane, radial around an axis, or kaleidoscope for both; it changes the layer contents permanently.
Repetition duplicates layers or groups by instancing with mirror, radial or kaleidoscope patterns. It is non-destructive and the instance count can be changed at any time.

A boolean needs at least two objects: a boolean object that carries the operation, and one or more targets it intersects. Operations are union, difference, intersection and split. Signed distance fields keep them fast, and a live boolean preview can be toggled.
Models are voxel grids of signed distance values, so layer resolution drives performance and memory use rather than polygon counts.
Primitives have shape and combine parameters, can be grouped and ordered, and can be converted to clay but not back.
Export can retopologise automatically: raw triangles, triangles or quads to a target count, with an adaptivity factor that raises density where detail is high.
Export can generate UVs, optionally spread across UDIM tiles up to a set maximum, when polygon type is UV-mapped triangles.
Exports USD and its variants USDA, USDC and USDZ, which carry meshes, lights, cameras and materials.
Exports glTF or GLB with meshes, lights, cameras and materials, with unit scale, up axis and instancing options.
Exports STL for 3D printing and CAD, which stores geometry only.
Exports VDB volumetric data of the kind used in simulation work.
The supported-formats table marks SMOD, FBX, OBJ, glTF/GLB, USD and VDB as importable and exportable; IGES, JT and STEP are import only.
capabilities.outputs: mesh in scene or exported file

capabilities.does: Works on the desktop and in VR on Meta Quest 2 and Quest Pro.

engines.name: Bake projects
engines.does: Bakes map types from high-poly to low-poly meshes using bake groups and cages.

engines.name: Python integration
engines.does: Scripting module with a tutorial and an API reference on the vendor site.

capabilities.does: Bake projects can output over 30 map types, among them tangent and object normals, height, position, curvature, convexity, cavity, thickness, bent normals, ambient occlusion, lighting passes, albedo, roughness, metalness and vertex colour.

capabilities.does: ID bakes give one colour per high-poly material, per material group, per object or per UV island.
capabilities.inputs: high-poly meshes with materials or groups

capabilities.does: Tangent-space and object-space normal maps are baked, with bent-normal variants that include baked ambient occlusion.

Render window modes: Raster, Hybrid (ray-traced lighting, separate denoising passes) and Ray Tracing (physically based light paths) with bounce counts, clamps, shadow offset, caustics and advanced light sampling.
Denoise mode with quality and strength controls; GPU mode needs a supported NVIDIA adapter, and Hybrid mode adds separate strengths for direct lighting, diffuse GI and specular.

Render passes include final composite, wireframe, geometry passes (alpha mask, depth, incidence, normals, position), ID passes, lighting passes and material value passes (albedo, emissive, gloss, metalness, roughness).
Render Cameras batch-render several cameras in one run, with add, enable and delete controls.
Video output uses the same core settings as stills plus compression quality; sequence formats write still images; transparency is not available for video files.
Sky lighting takes an image or procedural source with brightness, rotation and importance-sampling settings; backdrop modes are colour, sky, blurred sky and ambient sky.
Light types are directional, spot and omni; omni lights can have a sphere or rectangle shape whose size sets shadow softness. IES profiles can be imported, exported and saved in a library.
Texture Projects paint textures on a UV-mapped model in real time using layers and masks, linked to a material and to baked input maps.
capabilities.outputs: exported texture maps (normal maps in Y+ or Y-)

capabilities.does: Procedural layers: cellular, checkered, clouds, gradient, perlin, scatter (added in 5.03, non-destructive), tiles, turbulence and voronoi, for masks, grunge and surface patterns.
The Library holds smart materials and smart masks, plus brushes, materials, objects, scenes, skies and textures; a shared repository can be synced.
capabilities.outputs: preset applied to a texture project

capabilities.does: Decal layers and a decal tool place images onto a surface in texture projects.
The material texture module has UV, UDIM and triplanar modes.
capabilities.outputs: texture mapped by UV, UDIM tile or triplanar

capabilities.does: The material editor is built from modules: albedo, diffusion, transmission, reflection, microsurface, reflectivity, clearcoat, emission, occlusion, transparency, texture, displacement and surface.
Displacement module modes are height, vector and parallax.
The subsurface scattering module uses a scatter map, fuzz map and mask map with parameters such as scatter depth in mm, scatter colour, fuzz value and translucency approximation.
Skeletal animation can be imported; a keyframes window, timeline window and animation sets handle animation in the app.
A turntable animation page is listed in the animation section.
File types listed include USD, glTF, FBX, OBJ, COLLADA, Alembic, DXF, STL and PLY plus the native .tbscene.
Marmoset Viewer (.mview) is a listed file type; the product page names a Viewer for sharing scenes.
A Python integration exists; the docs page is a placeholder that points to an external scripting tutorial and the Python API reference.

engines.name: Python API
engines.does: Scripting interface with import, export and utility functions such as simulation quality presets.

capabilities.does: Simulation properties include a preset choice in place of the toolbar's simulation mode, Time Step, Simulations Per Frame (substeps within each time step), a conjugate-gradient option for solving large linear systems, and gravity.
Garments start as flat 2D panels. The user joins pattern edges as seams, places the pieces around an avatar and runs the simulation to see how they fit and drape.
In the 2D window a sewing line takes two clicks: first a segment of one pattern, then the matching segment of another. A length difference shows next to the cursor and turns red above 1 inch.
NVIDIA CUDA runs both GPU cloth simulation and GPU rendering; a system with only Intel or AMD graphics gets no GPU acceleration for simulation.
Brush Pinching pinches the cloth along brush strokes to add wrinkle-like detail; a pinching simulation override temporarily replaces global and fabric simulation values (release 2026.1).
Seamline Ripping Tool (beta) rips seamlines in real time under force and leaves frayed edges (release 2026.1).
Blend Shape Animation records changes to an avatar's blend shapes as animation keyframes (release 2026.1).

FBX import sets scale by value or unit, converts axes, can align objects to the ground and toggles joint animation and cameras. Export offers axis conversion and an animation range; only joints that arrived through FBX can be exported.
Alembic import and export are supported and carry vertex and animation data. Export options include weld or unweld of sewn vertices and thin or thick geometry.

USD import offers scale, start-position moves, replace-or-add loading and object types of avatar, trim or scene/prop. Export adds weld or unweld, thin or thick geometry, unified UVs with image size and seam fill, an animation range and optional garment simulation data.
OBJ import loads files as garment, trim or avatar; export can split objects, weld, add an alpha map, and write garment metadata as XML.
The Python API lists import functions (OBJ, FBX), export functions (OBJ, FBX, USD, Alembic, ZPac, thumbnails, snapshots) and utility calls such as setting simulation quality.
capabilities.outputs: automated import, export and simulation setup

capabilities.does: glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB) support arrived in version 2026.0 and covers import and export through the File menu. Export can write single or multiple objects, thickness, unified UVs, animation and embedded textures; the default unit is metres.
capabilities.inputs: glTF or VRM file, or garment

capabilities.does: Pattern Drafter, marked beta, offers two ways to start a first pattern: from measurement points, or from a flat sketch from which the program generates measurements. Its Match to Avatar Size option is marked 2026.1 and works only with default avatars.

The DNA importer reads a MetaHuman's Body and Head DNA files from the MetaHuman Editor through the File import menu and builds one combined avatar. It can add arrangement points and a fitting suit for humanoid avatars; .mtn motion files do not apply.
capabilities.inputs: MetaHuman Body and Head DNA files

outcomes: 3D garments for games, VFX and design

rea.notes: Version 2026.1 per the product page. System requirements: Windows 11, Apple silicon Macs; Linux only for enterprise customers on request. Licence page: standalone enterprise licence ended 2025-12-02. EULA not opened.

entries.name: SpeedTree

licence.name: commercial; terms not read

engines.name: SpeedTree Modeler
engines.does: Artist-focused procedural modelling of vegetation, paired with non-destructive manual editing and photogrammetry tools.

engines.name: Games and VFX export paths
engines.does: Separate export options optimised for real-time games and for film and animation.

engines.name: SpeedTree Runtime SDK
engines.does: Separate runtime SDK listed in the manual index.

capabilities.does: A generator hierarchy builds the model: a root Tree generator, Branch (trunks, branches, roots), Leaf mesh, Batched leaf, Frond, Zone and Card generators, each producing nodes with editable properties and variances.

Decorator generators add detail to branches: Cap closes open ends, Decal wraps a flat mesh for surface features, Fin makes thin flaps like fungus, Knot adds lumps or cavities, Shell wraps a parent in moss or vines.
Photogrammetry generators use scanned meshes in a tree: Mesh, Mesh converter, Stitch (joins native geometry to meshes) and Target (locates children precisely).

VFX wind mode simulates wind with a Fan object and per-generator properties; a Wind Wizard sets values, there are four branch wind levels, two leaf groups, frond wind and gusting, and results export as point caches.

Level of detail is set with LOD curves per generator: fewer segments, branch and frond removal by shrinking, leaf reduction with a Keep value, and up to three LOD meshes. Automatic LOD was a Games-edition feature in the version documented.
Export offers VFX and Games option sets, material or sequence export, command-line export, custom exporters, texture packing for games and packaging of .spm models with external assets.
Exports FBX among OBJ, USD, ST, STSDK, CGF, XML and Alembic, with games-ready textures, atlases and LODs, according to the vendor FAQ.
USD is listed as an export format for static meshes and point caches.
Alembic (.abc) is listed as an export format for point-cache wind and growth animation.
SpeedTree 10 adds a generator for physics-based vines with drooping and hanging behaviour.

In Freehand Mode the user picks Trim in the Property Bar, chooses a Trim Mode, holds the space bar and drags over the area to change. Modes include cut, shape and prune; extension-based models may need several swipes.
Spine rigs meshes from other DCC apps so static meshes get bones and movement settings inside SpeedTree.
The Cutout Editor assembles 2D leaf textures faster for building complex canopies.

outcomes: game-ready vegetation with LODs and wind
VFX trees with wind point caches

Generator and wind pages are from the SpeedTree 9 docs (docs9.speedtree.com) and the LOD page from the older docs.speedtree.com; the current latest version is SpeedTree 10 per the store FAQ. Platform and licence terms were not on the pages read. EULA not opened.

entries.name: SketchUp

licence.name: subscription: Go (web and iPad), Pro (adds desktop and LayOut), Studio (adds Revit import, V-Ray, point clouds)

engines.name: Ruby API
engines.does: Scripting API documented with YARD; it runs only from inside SketchUp on the main thread.

engines.name: LayOut
engines.does: 2D design documentation companion included from the Pro plan.

engines.name: V-Ray
engines.does: Photorealistic rendering add-on included in the Studio plan.

capabilities.does: Push/Pull (key P) turns a flat face into volume by dragging it out, or cuts into a solid by dragging it in. A typed distance sets exact depth; double-clicking another face repeats the move.
Follow Me extrudes a face along a path of connected edges. A basic version makes plain edges and faces; a procedural version makes an editable component. Automatic and manual path modes exist.
Solid tools: Outer Shell, Union, Subtract, Trim, Intersect and Split, with procedural variants of union, subtract and intersect that keep source solids editable. Inputs must be closed solids.
capabilities.inputs: two or more solid groups or components

capabilities.does: Components are reusable definitions; editing one instance updates all, while scaling or rotating an instance stays local. Adding attributes makes a Dynamic Component.
A scene stores camera position and field of view, visible tags, section planes, style and fog, shadow settings, environment and axes, and can be updated later.
Scenes play as an animation with transition and delay settings and export to MP4 (H.264), AVI, WebM, OGV or an image set, at 1080p, 720p, 480p or custom size, default 24 fps.
Section planes cut a model to show its inside, with one active cut per context, a fill option for closed slices, and export of section slices as DWG.
Match Photo sets the camera from a photo by dragging vanishing point bars along axes; the photo can be projected as a texture and used as a tracing reference.
capabilities.outputs: matched view, textured model, trace reference

capabilities.does: The Ruby API documentation is generated with YARD, links to tutorials, debugging and testing resources, and runs only inside SketchUp on the main thread.
Pro and Studio plans include Extension Warehouse access, and the Pro plan lists over 1000 extensions for tailored workflows.
LayOut is the 2D design documentation tool available with Pro and Studio.
3D Warehouse supplies ready-made models; daily and monthly download limits depend on the plan.
The Studio plan lists V-Ray, photorealistic visuals, rendered animations and 360-degree panoramas; all plans list photoreal materials.
Pro adds enhanced IFC and DWG compatibility; Studio imports Revit files.
Scan Essentials (Studio and Pro Scan) imports 3D point clouds so a model can be built on them and documented in 2D.

rea.notes: Studio desktop is stated as Windows only on the plans page; Pro desktop also shows Option-key modifiers for macOS in the help. Ruby API and a C SDK exist (C SDK not read). EULA not opened.

entries.name: Daz Studio

licence.name: free application with paid content and memberships (EULA not read)

engines.name: Software render engine
engines.does: CPU renderer used at the top render-quality level; exposes ray-trace depth, shadow samples and shading rate in the advanced page.

engines.name: Daz Script 2
engines.does: Scripting language bound to the Daz Studio API, built on Qt Script (ECMAScript), with object and action indexes.

engines.name: Bridges
engines.does: Plug-ins that send figures to Maya, 3ds Max, Blender, Cinema 4D, Unreal, Unity and Roblox.

capabilities.does: Pose Tool puts a free-rotate sphere and one ring per axis on a bone; Universal Tool moves, rotates and scales nodes. Rotation limits per bone can be switched off and restored.
Pinning options hold a bone in place softly: a pinned bone still gives way when another bone pulls on it.
capabilities.inputs: bones chosen in the Pose Tool

capabilities.does: Pose presets load by double-click, drag or context menu; saving a preset lets the user pick the properties, a single frame or an animated range, and compression.
capabilities.inputs: figure pose, property selection, frame range

capabilities.does: Face poses live in the Pose Controls property group under Head, with an Expressions group of complete expressions that can be mixed through sliders.
Shaping pane lists morph sliders grouped by body region; shaping presets save chosen morph values for the current frame or an animated range.
Region Navigator tool selects a body region by clicking the figure in the viewport, which opens the matching morph group in the Shaping pane.
Surfaces pane loads and saves material presets for the selected object; save options choose which surfaces and properties are stored.
Default shader exposes diffuse, specular, glossiness, ambient and opacity values with image-map slots, plus a per-surface UV set choice.
capabilities.inputs: colour values, image maps, UV set

capabilities.does: Surface properties include bump strength with minimum and maximum, and displacement strength with minimum and maximum, driven by image maps.
Spot Render tool renders only a marquee-selected part of the viewport so material and light changes can be checked quickly.
Four light types: distant (rotation only), spot (cone with spread angle), point, and linear point with falloff start and end spheres. Intensity above 100 percent is allowed.
Each light sets shadow type (none, deep shadow map, raytraced), softness and shadow samples; illumination can be limited to diffuse or specular.
Light presets save and load whole light setups, with options to replace all lights, replace selected ones or add; a three-point rig of key, fill and rim guides placement.
Render quality runs from an OpenGL preview up to a software render; advanced page sets max ray-trace depth, shadow samples and shading rate; full setting sets save as presets.
Render style switch chooses the scene materials or a cartoon look.
Camera properties set perspective on/off, focal length in mm, depth of field, focal distance and f-stop; orthographic and per-camera views are listed in the view menu.
Daz Script 2 extends Qt Script and reaches the scene hierarchy, geometry pipeline and actions; the reference has an object index, intrinsic types, samples and a script IDE pane.
Daz to Blender bridge exports static mesh, skeletal mesh, animation or environment, with optional morphs and baked subdivision, and a Blender add-on imports figures with morph sliders.
Open-source bridges for Unreal (C++) and Unity (C#) share a bridge utility library; the same GitHub organisation holds bridge repositories for Maya, Cinema 4D and Roblox.

formats.name: Daz native scene and content files
Blender file via Daz to Blender bridge

outcomes: assets sent to other DCC tools and game engines

engines.does: Poser render engine; its update notes mention transparent-object shadows.

engines.name: SuperFly
engines.does: Second render engine; update notes cover gobo spotlights and a Cycles shadow-blur setting.

engines.name: PoserCloth (Physics Room)
engines.does: Dynamic cloth simulation with fabric presets, a cloth-creator palette for Bullet cloth setup, and Python control.

capabilities.does: One-click cloth presets for silk, cotton, wool or fleece, denim, rubber and leather drape a garment on a figure.
Brush stiffness onto parts of a garment such as collars, cuffs, waistbands and seams to keep them rigid.
A Smooth button removes poke-through on the current frame and can be pressed repeatedly; an option smooths every frame automatically.
Dynamic garments follow the figure body and its morphs during animation; garments made for one figure can be fitted to a compatible figure, for example LaFemme 2 clothes on LaFemme 1.
Simulations with several animated constraints keep every constraint area active; saved cloth props reconnect to their figure on load, and simulations can be renamed or replaced.
Reference manual carries a Dynamic Hair topic that the 14.0.439 update corrected; dynamic hair is a Poser physics feature.
Python calls run cloth simulations without the interface: find a simulation by name, set frame range and rate, run CalculateDynamics, clear results with ClearDynamics.
Rectangle, square, circle and ellipse emitters, scaled in the property pane, give soft light shaped like the source.
An HDRI map lights the scene and serves as the background, wrapped as a sphere with 0 to 360 degree rotation.
Spotlights project patterns, textures or shapes through the beam (SuperFly).
Shadow blur radius under Cycles gives softer falloff, infinite lights have a wider blur radius, and transparent objects cast proper shadows in FireFly.
OpenGL 4.3 GLSL preview replaces the older Cg pipeline, shows up to 8 active lights, and previews Principled BSDF, Diffuse and Transparent BSDF, Math nodes and alpha textures.
Shaders can combine Principled BSDF, Diffuse BSDF, Transparent BSDF and Math nodes with alpha image textures and layering; the preview shows them since 14.0.372.
Pose saving is one click with default settings, a Simple or Advanced subset mode and filters for transforms; props can be included with position, rotation, scale, morphs and animation.
Rigs can be copied across the symmetry plane without distortion.
Poser 14 ships with over 30 GB of included content: legacy figures, many updated for SuperFly, with morphs, poses and materials.

scripting: Python (Poser Python Shell and PoserCloth calls)
outcomes: still renders and animations of posed figures

capabilities.does: Motion Director steers a character by mouse waypoints, WASD keys, gamepad, path, zone or follow modes; Motion Record writes the result to the timeline.
capabilities.inputs: input device, target path or zone

capabilities.does: AccuLips builds a viseme track from recorded voice, text-to-speech or an audio file, with a lips editor, smoothing, an editable English dictionary and 16 talking styles.
Crowd tools use a navigation mesh and walkways to scatter actors, with smart avoidance, flock mode, ambient animation groups and prop distribution.
Curve Editor edits rotation, translation and scale curves with Auto, Smooth, Spline, Linear, Step, Accelerate and Decelerate tangents, break and unify handles, and 16 curve presets.
Alembic import and export carries baked point-cache animation, including soft cloth and hair, with current-frame, range or all export; one material per mesh only.
Characters from Maya or 3ds Max convert in through FBX; a batch FBX export writes characters, props and cameras together.
Real-time renderer with PBR shading and post effects keeps one look across iClone, game engines and design tools.
Motion blur has adjustable intensity and frame blending.
Mirror plane shader fakes reflective floors, windows, mirrors and screens with adjustable strength and clarity.
Motion LIVE combines Vicon, Rokoko, Xsens, OptiTrack and iPhone data to capture face, body and hands at once in real time.
Motion retargeting adapts a clip to characters of other proportions.

Live Face streams iPhone face tracking to a character and adds a smoothing filter, a multiplier for the tracked values and live retargeting. A separate AI mocap feature tracks faces from live or recorded video and can sync lip and tongue motion to a voice.
ExPlus blendshapes, scan-based, cover mouth, cheek, brow, eye and tongue motion.
Facial animation page names muscle-based face key editing and puppet-style emotive expressions as the hand-animation route, next to lip-sync and mocap.
PhysX-based rigid body and kinematic physics are listed in the feature comparison.
NVIDIA PhysX soft cloth simulation is listed among the real-time production features, next to rigid-body physics.
Free Auto Setup plug-ins import iClone assets into Unreal Engine, Unity, Blender, Maya, 3ds Max and Marmoset Toolbag with materials and skeletons arranged.
Unreal Live Link (paid) and MetaHuman Live Link (free) stream animation to Unreal Engine; an Omniverse connector adds iClone to NVIDIA Omniverse.
Video Mocap add-on turns plain video into animated characters.
Motion Planning add-on (paid) defines agent behaviours in a node graph for simulation.
BuildingGen add-on (paid) generates 3D buildings procedurally.
PopcornFX add-on (paid) brings real-time particle effects.
The feature comparison table has a Python API row, and the add-ons section says iClone can be extended through its Python scripting API; the page gives no further detail.

A character can be sent to ZBrush or Blender and a sculpted morph returns with one click; OBJ from other tools also imports as a shape.
HD morphs add bone structure, muscle, skin folds and wrinkles on top of general shapes; partial and full-body HD sliders cover ageing and weight; 300 base morphs are embedded.
SkinGen stacks skin layers (normal effects, details, blemishes, acquired marks) and makeup layers; free tier caps layers at 15 with four blend modes; output up to 4K per body material.
Smart Hair builds hair, beard and brows from card-based elements combined into groups and styles, with a mesh editor, vertex-assignment tool and scalp and baby-hair patches.
Dynamic fitting and selective conformation make clothing follow body morphs; rigid details such as buttons can follow either the garment or the body.
Auto skin-weight transfer rigs an imported garment or accessory in one click from a garment category preset.
Soft cloth physics uses weight maps, collision volumes and wind response, selectable from presets.
Shrink Wrap settings (shrink intensity, tuck-in blend range) fit outer garments over inner ones.
Mesh editing selects by vertex, face or element and edge loops to remove inner faces and smooth or restore distorted areas on AI-made or imported meshes.
AccuRIG rigs A-pose or T-pose humanoid meshes (single or multi-mesh, partial rigging), with bone masking, joint placement, skin weight refinement, hard-surface attachment and reusable bone profiles.
HD facial profile gives 262 blendshapes and 128 corrective morphs, driven by Face Puppet and Face Key editors, Motion LIVE, AccuFace and MetaHuman Animator.
ActorMIXER blends facial features and body parts from library or own characters on a wheel, creates relatives, random characters and packages mixer sets.
Headshot 3 builds a head from one photo (topology refinement, lens correction, texture reprojection) or wraps a scanned or sculpted head mesh and bakes textures.
Auto Setup assigns shaders and skeletons in Unreal and Unity, with add-ons for Blender, Maya, 3ds Max and Marmoset Toolbag; ZBrush models convert to animatable characters.
USD export creates animated digital humans for NVIDIA Omniverse.
CC5 characters share facial controls and skeleton layout with MetaHuman; AutoSetup and LiveLink stream animation between CC, iClone and Unreal.

entries.name: Cascadeur

licence.name: Free (no commercial use), Indie, Pro, Teams, Educational and Pro Trial licence types

engines.name: AutoPhysics
engines.does: Physics solver that analyses a keyed animation using centre of mass and fulcrum points and proposes a physically plausible version.

engines.name: AutoPosing
engines.does: Pose predictor that moves the whole rig when a few controllers are dragged.

engines.name: Python scripting (csc module)
engines.does: Python 3.8 API with app, scene, viewer and editor modules and a user command folder.

capabilities.does: AutoPosing predicts a full-body pose while the user moves a few active controllers (humanoids; quadrupeds in Pro); fixed, locked, additional and direction controllers refine it. It overwrites existing poses on the current keyframe.

AutoPhysics shows a coloured copy of the character with a physically plausible version of the animation (green fine, red unfixable, blue stale) and Snap to AutoPhysics writes it back; keep-rotation and keep-translation sliders control strength.

Ballistic curve for the airborne centre of mass is shaped by an impulse point, height point and landing point, with gravity, velocity and cut-off height in properties; a snap button fits the animation to it.

Ragdoll simulates the rig rigid bodies between two keyframes with stiffness, damping, gravity, floor friction and bounce, angle constraints and collision shapes; Snap to AutoPhysics applies the result.
Retargeting copies animation between two AutoPosing rigs with different proportions via Edit retargeting copy and paste; root motion correction can be turned off to keep foot sliding.
Mocap (alpha) reads poses from an mp4 reference video, one keyframe per selected timeline frame; single actor only; first use downloads a model of about 700 MB.

Graph Editor edits animation curves of exposed channels with Linear, Step, Fixed and Bezier Clamped interpolation, break and unify tangents, reset tangents and auto smooth; it has no filter or scale tools.

Tween Machine blends current positions with positions from nearby frames using previous/next, inertial or interpolation filters, in global, local or relative mode, with a slider and relaxation setting.
Trajectories draw the path of selected objects over an interval; Trajectory Edit Mode moves path points with manipulators, and relative-to-pivot mode shows motion about another point.

Animation Unbaking turns a fully keyed (baked) clip into few keyframes with mixed interpolation, using settings for interpolation difference, AutoPosing precision and finger tolerance; works per animation track.
Quick Rigging Tool maps joints to a humanoid or quadruped template, optional twist joints, mirror pairs, Spline IK and hinge logic, then Generate rig finishes the control rig.
Spline IK creates a curve driving a joint chain between a chosen first and last joint, with point controllers at the curve ends; suited to tails and long chains.
Inbetweening generates motion between at least two keyframes on a selected interval (keys up to 120 frames apart) from the key poses.

Motion Generation builds animation from a trajectory and start/end keys with style (walk, run, acrobatic), key, head-direction, trajectory and reference forces; output is baked with fixed interpolation.
Ghosts draw silhouettes of the character on previous, next, both or timeline-selected frames, optionally keyframes only, with outlines and a frame count.
Fulcrum points are found automatically where a controller is near a collider and barely moves; per-controller state (Fulcrum, Enforce, NotFulcrum), collision radius and max speed tune it.
Secondary motion refines AutoPhysics output, with per-controller local and global blending, damping and air friction, plus gravity and floor collision settings; applied through Snap to Physics.
Python 3.8 scripts import the csc module; app, scene manager, viewers and editors read and change objects, and a command file with command_name() and run(scene) adds a menu entry.
The help index has import and export guides for FBX and DAE, with sub-guides for Unreal, Unity, Blender, Daz Studio and other tools; separate guides cover USD and GLB/GLTF.
USD import and export guides exist in the help index and the home page lists USD as a supported format.
Live Link for Unreal Engine streams Cascadeur animation to an Unreal scene; named in the help index and on the home page.
Help index has export guides for Unreal Engine and Unity, plus import guides for Mixamo rigs, MetaHumans, Daz Studio and Character Creator characters.

engines.name: PBR vertex painting
engines.does: Colour, roughness, metalness and opacity are stored in vertices, so painting needs no UVs.

capabilities.does: Brush set: Clay, Brush, Smooth, Layer (height-limited), Inflate, Nudge, Stamp (alpha shaped), Flatten, Planar, Crease, Pinch, plus Move and Drag deformation tools.
Mask paints protection onto vertices against sculpting and painting; SelMask does the same through selection controls.
Multiresolution subdivides a mesh into levels you can edit separately: subdivide, reverse, delete lower or higher levels, linear subdivision, sharp border, lock level 0.
Voxel remesher rebuilds topology at uniform density with a resolution value, optional multiresolution build and sharp-edge keeping.
Dynamic topology adds and removes faces locally while sculpting or painting; detail by screen, radius or constant, method uniformisation, subdivision or decimation, and masked-area protection.
Decimation reduces triangles toward a target count while trying to keep detail, with options to preserve painting, uniform faces and borders.
Quad remesh builds clean quad topology from a target quad count, crease angle and hole-fill limit; a separate Quad Remesher tool gives more control on iOS and desktop.
Two unwrap methods: UVAtlas (more islands, less distortion; max stretch and spacing) and BFF (fewer cuts, more distortion; cone count).

Bake projects other visible objects or a high-res source into the selected object UVs to make normal, roughness, metalness, colour, emissive and opacity maps, with cage radius and ray offset; vertex paint can also be reprojected.
PBR vertex painting stores colour, roughness, metalness and opacity per vertex; textures can replace a channel, and layers and masks limit Paint All.
Layers hold sculpt and paint offsets with visibility, Photoshop-style blend modes, channel factors, offset strength, mask-from-channel and extract with fill, shell or layer-difference closing.
Symmetry with planes and radial repeats, local or world method; mirroring copies one side to the other, split-and-mirror cuts and welds, flip swaps sides.
Holes tool closes gaps (detail, fill non-manifold) and Force Manifold removes non-manifold edges and tiny faces.
Tube builds a tube from a drawn curve; Lathe makes a revolved surface from a drawn profile; Insert places an object on another surface.
Trim removes a selected region with options to fill the gap, Split keeps the removed part as a new object, Project moves vertices to a selection without adding geometry.
OBJ, PLY and STL import and export; native .nom project files; Add to scene merges a project into the current one.
FBX imports (marked experimental) and exports.
USD export is offered next to glTF, OBJ, PLY, STL, FBX and NOM export.
glTF/GLB import and export.

Nomad exports several mesh formats, including STL, OBJ, glTF/GLB and USD. Its feature table says STL keeps only vertex colors, while OBJ also keeps quads, objects, face groups and textures. The page does not mention 3D printing.
Render exports an image combining the project lights, materials and post-processing.

engines.does: Separate 2D canvas for interfaces and animated graphics that shares the interaction model.

capabilities.does: AI 3D generation makes models from a text prompt, a reference image or both, through image previews first, with a choice of models (Hunyuan3D, Hunyuan 3.1 Pro, Trellis 2, Meshy) and credit cost shown beforehand.
Boolean objects union, subtract or intersect selected 3D objects, can be nested and changed later; Merge Geometries joins objects into one geometry.
Sculpting on a primitive in edit mode with Grab, Draw, Draw Clay and Smooth brushes; radius, strength and a subdivision setting control the result.

Physics per object: positioned or dynamic bodies, weight, gravity scale, friction, damping, bounce, translation and rotation constraints and collider precision; scene gravity set in the Simulation panel.
Emitters with plane, box, sphere, torus, cone or custom shape; birth rate, lifetime, speed, colour blend, curl/simplex/fbm noise, colliders, attractors and vortex force objects, and presets.
Cloner modifier duplicates an object in radial, linear, grid or object-surface patterns; a Randomness layer adds noise-based transform variation that can be animated.
Timeline records edits as keyframes on animatable properties (position, rotation, scale, size, material, opacity, cloner, path alignment); several timelines can be added per scene.
Graph Editor reshapes speed and easing of keyframes by editing the animation curves.
Objects get a Base State and extra states that change scale, position, rotation or colour; in Play Mode they react once events and actions are added.
Drag-and-drop import of .ply splats from Polycam and Luma splat files; box or sphere crop areas can permanently remove splats; no physics, cloner or lighting on splats.
Each material is built from stacked layers that share opacity and blend settings. A new object starts with a Color layer and a Lighting layer, and 3D objects default to Phong lighting.
Public URL for sharing a scene, and embed code for tools such as Notion, Webflow, WordPress and Framer.
Code API for web: npm packages runtime (vanilla JS), react-spline and Next.js support; read or set variables and properties, trigger transitions and listen to events.
Cloud files with simultaneous editing, comments, link or email invitations as editor or viewer, workspaces, projects and version history.
File export includes glTF/GLB, together with USDZ, STL, images, image sequences and video.
USDZ file export for Apple AR; native 3D embeds also target SwiftUI/visionOS and Kotlin/Android.
A timeline exports as video by picking the timeline, duration, frame rate and resolution.

engines.does: Browser editor with Design mode (modifiers, deformers), Edit mode (polygon tools), materials and a 3D configurator interaction builder.

capabilities.does: Array modifiers repeat an object linearly, radially, in a grid or across the surface of another object.
Subdivide modifier splits geometry into smaller pieces for a denser mesh.
Bevel modifier rounds sharp corners with angled edges.
Symmetry modifier mirrors an object across a chosen axis.
Boolean modifier combines two objects by union, subtraction or intersection.
Deformers bend, twist, taper, skew, stretch, spherify and add noise along an axis, with area of effect set to unlimited, limited or within a box.

The Simplify deformer lowers the geometric complexity of an object while keeping its overall form. Its calculations take significant resources, so a deformer can be converted into fixed geometry to avoid recalculation; that conversion matters in Studio only.
Edit mode extrude pushes a selected face or edge outward.
Edit mode adds Bridge (join edge loops), Cut, Slide, Draw, Merge faces and Mesh Tools for refining geometry.
Advanced material layers add subsurface, refraction, clearcoat, thin film, reflectivity and double-sided rendering to the basic PBR set.
Baking stores ambient occlusion or lightmap results in textures at 256 to 4096 px or auto size, with draft, medium or high sample counts and optional denoise; UV0 or UV1; runs on the CPU.
Export GLB (single file) or glTF (JSON plus textures).
USDZ export gives one lightweight AR file with embedded textures for Apple AR.
FBX import and export; animation limited to transform and skeletal types.
STL export carries geometry only, for 3D printing.
CAD formats IGES and STEP can be imported on the Business plan only.
SPLAT and PLY Gaussian splat files import as scene assets.

No-code interactions combine triggers (on load, click, hover, drag, event, WebXR), optional conditions and actions (animation, materials, variants, camera, sound, visibility, AR, send event, set variable).
Model API (Business plan) controls an embedded scene from page script: variants, materials, textures, camera, animation, objects, import and export to GLB, GLTF, FBX, USDZ.

Image to 3D model builds a textured model from a dropped image using a choice of generator models (Hunyuan, Tripo, Trellis, Meshy, Rodin, Pixal); output can be simplified and edited; monthly generation limits apply.

engines.name: CGA shape grammar
engines.does: Rule language that refines start shapes into detailed building models with operations such as extrude, split and texture.

engines.name: Dynamic city layouts
engines.does: Street network editor whose changes rebuild dependent geometry on the fly.

capabilities.does: Rules in a .cga file refine a start shape step by step into a detailed model; the rules work on shapes with a scope (oriented bounding box).
Pipeline from street network to blocks, lots and CGA-built buildings; any stage can be imported instead of generated.
Interactive street networks with sidewalks and blocks; geometry that depends on the layout, such as buildings, rebuilds while street width is edited.
Rules with random parameters give varied buildings; the random seed can change for all buildings or single ones.
Rule parameters can be overwritten per building without editing the rule file.
The split operation cuts a shape along an x, y or z scope axis, or along u or v in texture space, into parts with absolute, relative or floating sizes; a repeat switch fills the scope.
The comp operation divides a shape into faces, edges, vertices, groups, materials or holes, chosen by selectors such as front, top, border, ridge, street.front or tags.
The texture operation sets the colour map, and the opacity map when the image has alpha, for the current shape from an image file.
Python scripting automates repeated tasks and report creation in the editor.
A script-based export runs arbitrary Python commands during a batch export.
FBX export for Maya, 3ds Max and MotionBuilder with layered textures and per-texture UVW transforms.
glTF export with PBR materials and instancing; the page calls it the recommended exchange format for new projects.
USD export stores large scenes with little loss and supports instancing, multitexture and referencing.
Alembic export for VFX pipelines, with instancing and multitexture.
Datasmith export moves models into Unreal Engine and Twinmotion with PBR materials and geometry instancing.
IFC export (version 2x3 only) describes building elements for BIM and CAD use; DWG and COLLADA export also exist.
